title.raw: 卷一百九十一 列傳第一百四十一: 方伎 Volume 191 Biographies 141: The Arts

sentences.zh: 崔善為 薛頤 甄權弟:立言 宋俠 許胤宗 乙弗弘禮 袁天綱 孫思邈 明崇儼 張憬藏 李嗣真 張文仲附:李虔縱 韋慈藏 尚獻甫附:裴知古 孟詵 嚴善思 金梁鳳 張果 葉法善 僧玄奘 僧神秀附:慧能 普寂 義福 僧一行附:泓師 桑道茂

translations.literal: Cui Shanwei, Xue Yi, Zhen Quan with younger brother Liyan, Song Xia, Xu Yinzong, Yifu Hongli, Yuan Tiangang, Sun Simiao, Ming Chongyan, Zhang Jingzang, Li Sizhen, Zhang Wenzong with appended: Li Qianzong, Wei Cizang, Shang Xianfu with appended: Pei Zhigu, Meng Shen, Yan Shansi, Jin Liangfeng, Zhang Guo, Ye Fashan, the monk Xuanzang, the monk Shenxiu with appended: Huineng, Puji, Yifu, the monk Yixing with appended: Hongshi, Sang Daomao
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shanwei; Xue Yi; Zhen Quan, with his younger brother Liyan; Song Xia; Xu Yinzong; Yifu Hongli; Yuan Tiangang; Sun Simiao; Ming Chongyan; Zhang Jingzang; Li Sizhen; Zhang Wenzong, with appended biographies of Li Qianzong and Wei Cizang; Shang Xianfu, with appended biographies of Pei Zhigu; Meng Shen; Yan Shansi; Jin Liangfeng; Zhang Guo; Ye Fashan; the monk Xuanzang; the monk Shenxiu, with appended biographies of Huineng, Puji, and Yifu; the monk Yixing, with appended biography of Hongshi; and Sang Daomao

sentences.zh: 夫術數占相之法，出於陰陽家流。

translations.literal: As for the methods of numerology and divination by physiognomy, they issue from the school of Yin and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: The arts of numerology, divination, and physiognomy arose from the Yin–Yang school of thought.

sentences.zh: 自劉向演《洪範》之言，京房傳焦贛之法，莫不望氣視祲，懸知災異之來；

translations.literal: From Liu Xiang's exposition of the words of the Hongfan through Jing Fang's transmission of Jiao Gan's methods, none failed to observe vapors and inspect omens, foreknowing in advance the coming of calamities and anomalies;
translations.idiomatic: From Liu Xiang's elaboration of the Great Plan through Jing Fang's transmission of Jiao Gan's techniques, practitioners alike watched the qi of heaven, read portents in the sky, and claimed to foresee disasters before they arrived;

sentences.zh: 運策揲蓍，預定吉凶之會。

translations.literal: They manipulated rods and plucked yarrow stalks, predetermining the conjunctions of fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: they cast stalks and counted yarrow, seeking to fix in advance whether fortune or misfortune would meet them.

sentences.zh: 固已詳于魯史，載彼《周官》。

translations.literal: This was already set forth in detail in the history of Lu and recorded in the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Such practices were already treated at length in the chronicles of Lu and enshrined in the Offices of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 其弊者肄業非精，順非行偽，而庸人不修德義，妄冀遭逢。

translations.literal: The abuse lay in pursuing the craft without mastery, following what was not the Way and practicing deceit, while mediocre men did not cultivate virtue and righteousness yet vainly hoped for a lucky turn of fate.
translations.idiomatic: The abuse came when men pursued the craft without real mastery, cloaked false conduct in orthodox formulas, and ordinary people, neglecting virtue, vainly hoped fate would favor them.

sentences.zh: 如魏豹之納薄姬，孫皓之邀青蓋，王莽隨式而移坐，劉歆聞讖而改名。

translations.literal: Such as Wei Bao taking Lady Bo Ji, Sun Hao welcoming the green-canopied carriage, Wang Mang shifting his seat according to the pattern, and Liu Xin changing his name upon hearing a prophecy.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bao took Lady Bo because of a prophecy; Sun Hao courted the green-canopied carriage of surrender; Wang Mang moved his seat to follow an omen; Liu Xin changed his name when he heard a prognostication.

sentences.zh: 近者綦連耀之構異端，蘇玄明之犯宮禁，皆因占候，輔此奸凶。

translations.literal: Recently Qi Lianyao's founding of heterodox teachings and Su Xuanming's violation of palace prohibitions both relied on divination and observation of omens, aiding such traitors and villains.
translations.idiomatic: More recently, Qi Lianyao's heterodox plotting and Su Xuanming's breach of the palace gates both drew on astrological divination to abet treachery.

sentences.zh: 聖王禁星緯之書，良有以也。

translations.literal: That sage kings banned books on stars and weft-omens was truly for good reason.
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers had good reason to ban books of star lore and celestial omens.

sentences.zh: 國史載袁天綱前知武后，恐匪格言，而李淳風刪方伎書，備言其要。

translations.literal: The dynastic history records that Yuan Tiangang foreknew the Empress Wu, fearing this was not a proper saying, yet Li Chunfeng, in editing books on the arts, set forth the essentials in full.
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic history notes that Yuan Tiangang foresaw Empress Wu—a passage some feared was not fit moral teaching—yet when Li Chunfeng edited the treatises on the arts, he recorded the essentials in full.

sentences.zh: 舊本錄崔善為已下，此深於其術者，兼桑門道士方伎等，並附此篇。

translations.literal: The old edition recorded from Cui Shanwei downward those deeply versed in these arts, together with Buddhist monks, Daoist priests, and practitioners of the arts, all appended in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier edition listed from Cui Shanwei onward those most accomplished in these arts, together with Buddhist monks, Daoist priests, and other practitioners, all gathered in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 崔善為

translations.literal: Cui Shanwei
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shanwei

sentences.zh: 崔善為，貝州武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Shanwei was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shanwei was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖顒，後魏員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yong was an Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yong served as an extraordinary attendant of the scattered cavalry in Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父權會，齊丞相府參軍事。

translations.literal: His father Quanhui was a staff officer in the chief minister's office of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quanhui was a staff officer in the chief minister's office of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 善為好學，兼善天文算曆，明達時務。

translations.literal: Shanwei loved learning and was also skilled in astronomy, mathematics, and calendrics, with clear understanding of affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Shanwei was devoted to learning and equally skilled in astronomy, mathematics, and calendrics, with a keen grasp of contemporary affairs.

sentences.zh: 弱冠州舉，授文林郎。

translations.literal: At his capping age he was nominated by the province and appointed Gentleman of the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: At his coming of age he was nominated by the province and appointed Gentleman of the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 屬隋文帝營仁壽宮，善為領丁匠五百人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was building Renshou Palace, Shanwei led five hundred corvée laborers and artisans.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui built Renshou Palace, Shanwei supervised five hundred corvée laborers and artisans.

sentences.zh: 右僕射楊素為總監，巡至善為之所，索簿點人，善為手持簿暗唱之，五百人一無差失，素大驚。

translations.literal: The Right Vice Director Yang Su served as chief overseer; when he toured to Shanwei's section and demanded the register to count the men, Shanwei held the register and recited from it from memory—all five hundred without a single error. Su was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, vice director of the right, served as chief overseer. When he came to Shanwei's section and demanded the roster to count the men, Shanwei held the register and recited every name from memory—not one of the five hundred was wrong. Yang Su was astonished.

sentences.zh: 自是有四方疑獄，多使善為推按，無不妙盡其理。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever doubtful cases arose from the four quarters, Shanwei was often sent to investigate them, and none failed to be brilliantly resolved to their full rationale.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever doubtful legal cases came from the provinces, Shanwei was often assigned to investigate them, and he invariably unraveled each to its root.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，稍遷樓煩郡司戶書佐。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era he was gradually promoted to clerk of the revenue section in Loufan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou reign he was promoted to clerk of the revenue section in Loufan commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖時為太守，甚禮遇之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was regional inspector, he treated Shanwei with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was still a regional inspector, he treated Shanwei with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 善為以隋政傾頹，乃密勸進，高祖深納之。

translations.literal: Shanwei, seeing Sui government tottering, secretly urged Gaozu to advance; Gaozu deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Sui regime crumbling, Shanwei secretly urged Gaozu to rise in rebellion, and Gaozu took his counsel to heart.

sentences.zh: 義旗建，引為大將軍府司戶參軍，封清河縣公。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, he was brought in as revenue staff officer in the Grand General's headquarters and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe county.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was launched, he was appointed revenue staff officer in the Grand General's headquarters and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 武德中，曆內史舍人、尚書左丞，甚得譽。

translations.literal: During the Wude era he successively served as Secretariat drafter and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, winning great renown.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era he served as Secretariat drafter and then as left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, earning wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 諸曹令史惡其聰察，因其身短而傴，嘲之曰：「崔子曲知鉤，隨例得封侯。

translations.literal: The clerks of the various bureaus resented his keen perception; because his body was short and stooped, they mocked him, saying: "Young Cui, crooked as a hook, gets a marquisate by routine.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks of the various bureaus resented his sharp scrutiny. Because he was short and stooped, they mocked him with a verse: "Young Cui, bent like a hook, wins a marquisate by routine.

sentences.zh: 髆上全無項，胸前別有頭。」

translations.literal: Above the shoulders there is no neck at all; on the chest there is a separate head."
translations.idiomatic: Above the shoulders he has no neck; on his chest he wears a second head."

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，勞勉之曰：「澆薄之人，醜正惡直。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of this, he comforted and encouraged him, saying: "Shallow and base men hate what is upright and detest what is straight.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard of this, he comforted Shanwei, saying: "Petty men always hate what is upright and detest what is straight.

sentences.zh: 昔齊末奸吏歌斛律明月，而高緯愚暗，遂滅其家。

translations.literal: In former times, at the end of Qi, wicked clerks sang songs against Hulu Guang, and Gao Wei, foolish and benighted, thereby destroyed his household.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Northern Qi, corrupt clerks spread songs defaming Hulu Guang, and the foolish Emperor Gao Wei destroyed his entire family.

sentences.zh: 朕雖不德，倖免斯事。」

translations.literal: Though I lack virtue, I have fortunately escaped such a thing."
translations.idiomatic: Though I lack virtue, I have been spared that fate."

sentences.zh: 因購流言者，使加其罪。

translations.literal: He then offered a reward for the slanderers and had their crimes increased.
translations.idiomatic: He then posted a reward for the slanderers and had them punished more severely.

sentences.zh: 時傅仁均所撰《戊寅元曆》，議者紛然，多有同異，李淳風又駁其短十有八條。

translations.literal: At the time Fu Renjun's Wuyin Origin Calendar was under debate; disputants were clamorous, with many agreements and disagreements, and Li Chunfeng further refuted its shortcomings in eighteen articles.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Renjun's Wuyin Origin Calendar was then under heated debate, with many points of agreement and dispute, and Li Chunfeng added eighteen refutations of its errors.

sentences.zh: 高祖令善為考校二家得失，多有駁正。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered Shanwei to examine and compare the strengths and weaknesses of the two sides, and he made many corrections and refutations.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered Shanwei to compare the two sides' arguments, and he offered many corrections.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，拜陝州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed prefect of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he was appointed prefect of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷立議，戶殷之處，得徙寬鄉。

translations.literal: At the time the court had proposed that in districts with dense households, people might be relocated to districts with spare land.
translations.idiomatic: The court had proposed that people in densely populated districts be allowed to move to districts with spare land.

sentences.zh: 善為上表稱：「畿內之地，是謂戶殷，丁壯之人，悉入軍府。

translations.literal: Shanwei submitted a memorial stating: 'The lands within the capital region are what is called densely settled; able-bodied men are all enrolled in military households.
translations.idiomatic: Shanwei submitted a memorial arguing: 'The capital region is already densely settled, and every able-bodied man is enrolled in the military households.

sentences.zh: 若聽移轉，便出關外。

translations.literal: If relocation is permitted, they will leave beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: If relocation is permitted, they will simply move beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 此則虛近實遠，非經通之議。」

translations.literal: This would empty what is near and fill what is far—no policy consonant with enduring principle."
translations.idiomatic: That would hollow out what is near while strengthening what is far—a policy at odds with sound governance."

sentences.zh: 其事乃止。

translations.literal: The matter was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 後曆大理、司農二卿，名為稱職。

translations.literal: He later successively served as minister of the Court of Judicial Review and minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, renowned as competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as minister of judicial review and then minister of the imperial granaries, and in both posts was regarded as thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 坐與少卿不協，出為秦州刺史，卒，贈刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Because he did not get along with a vice minister, he was sent out as prefect of Qinzhou; he died, and was posthumously awarded Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After a falling-out with a vice minister, he was posted out as prefect of Qinzhou. He died there and was posthumously awarded Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 薛頤，滑州人也。

translations.literal: Xue Yi was a native of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yi was a native of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為道士。

translations.literal: During the Daye era he became a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he became a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 解天文律曆，尤曉雜占。

translations.literal: He understood astronomy, pitch pipes, and calendrics, and was especially versed in miscellaneous divination.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered astronomy, pitch pipes, and calendrics and was especially skilled in miscellaneous divination.

sentences.zh: 煬帝引入內道場，亟令章醮。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang brought him into the inner Daoist sanctuary and repeatedly ordered him to perform liturgical offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang brought him into the inner Daoist sanctuary and repeatedly ordered him to perform ritual offerings.

sentences.zh: 武德初，追直秦府。

translations.literal: Early in Wude he was summoned to serve on duty at the Prince of Qin's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era he was summoned to serve at the Prince of Qin's establishment.

sentences.zh: 頤嘗密謂秦王曰：「德星守秦分，王當有天下，願王自愛。」

translations.literal: Yi once secretly told the Prince of Qin: "The Virtue Star guards the Qin asterism; Your Highness is destined to possess the realm. I pray Your Highness take care of yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Yi once told the Prince of Qin in secret: "The Virtue Star holds the Qin asterism—you are destined to rule the realm. I urge you to take care of yourself."

sentences.zh: 秦王乃奏授太史丞，累遷太史令。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin then memorialized to appoint him Vice Director of the Astrographic Bureau, and he was promoted in stages to Director.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then recommended him for appointment as vice director of the Astrographic Bureau, and he rose in stages to director.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，太宗將封禪泰山，有彗星見，頤因言「考諸玄象，恐未可東封」。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, when Taizong was about to perform the Feng and Shan rites on Mount Tai, a comet appeared; Yi therefore said, 'Considering the dark signs of heaven, I fear the eastern rite may not yet be feasible.'
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era, when Taizong planned to perform the Feng and Shan rites on Mount Tai, a comet appeared. Yi said, 'Judging by the celestial signs, I fear the eastern rite is not yet auspicious.'

sentences.zh: 會褚遂良亦言其事，於是乃止。

translations.literal: It happened that Chu Suiliang also spoke on the matter, and the rite was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang spoke to the same effect, and the rite was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 頤後上表請為道士，太宗為置紫府觀於九秬山，拜頤中大夫，行紫府觀主事。

translations.literal: Later Yi submitted a memorial requesting to become a Daoist priest; Taizong established the Purple Mansion Abbey on Mount Jiuju, appointed Yi Grand Master of Palace Attendance, and made him acting abbot of the Purple Mansion Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Yi later petitioned to become a Daoist priest. Taizong founded the Purple Mansion Abbey on Mount Jiuju, appointed Yi grand master of palace attendance, and made him acting abbot of the abbey.

sentences.zh: 又敕於觀中建一清台，候玄象，有災祥薄蝕謫見等事，隨狀聞奏。

translations.literal: He also ordered a Pure Observatory built within the abbey to watch the dark signs of heaven; whenever there were calamities, auspices, thinness, eclipses, or demotions and appearances, reports were submitted according to circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered a Pure Observatory built at the abbey to watch the heavens; whenever calamities, auspicious signs, eclipses, or unusual celestial appearances occurred, Yi was to report them at once.

sentences.zh: 前後所奏，與京台李淳風多相符契。

translations.literal: His memorials before and after largely agreed with Li Chunfeng of the capital observatory.
translations.idiomatic: His reports largely agreed with those of Li Chunfeng at the capital observatory.

sentences.zh: 後數歲卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years later.

sentences.zh: 甄權，許州扶溝人也。

translations.literal: Zhen Quan was a native of Fugou in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Quan was a native of Fugou in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗以母病，與弟立言專醫方，得其旨趣。

translations.literal: Once, because his mother was ill, he and his younger brother Liyan devoted themselves to medical formulas and grasped their essential principles.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he and his younger brother Liyan devoted themselves to medicine and mastered its essentials.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，為秘書省正字，後稱疾免。

translations.literal: Early in Kaihuang of Sui he served as proofreader in the Secretariat, later pleading illness to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era of Sui he served as a Secretariat proofreader, then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 隋魯州刺史庫狄鏚苦風患，手不得引弓，諸醫莫能療。

translations.literal: Kudi Lei, regional inspector of Lu in Sui, suffered from wind ailment and could not draw a bow with his hand; no physician could cure him.
translations.idiomatic: Kudi Lei, regional inspector of Lu under Sui, suffered from a wind disorder that left him unable to draw a bow; no physician could cure him.

sentences.zh: 權謂曰：「但將弓箭向垛，一針可以射矣。」

translations.literal: Quan told him: "Simply take bow and arrow toward the butt; one needle will enable you to shoot."
translations.idiomatic: Quan told him: "Take your bow and arrow toward the target—one needle will let you shoot again."

sentences.zh: 針其肩隅一穴，應時即射。

translations.literal: He needled one point at the corner of his shoulder, and immediately he shot.
translations.idiomatic: He needled a point at the corner of the shoulder, and the patient shot at once.

sentences.zh: 權之療疾，多此類也。

translations.literal: Quan's treatment of illness was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Quan's cures were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十七年，權年一百三歲，太宗幸其家，視其飲食，訪以藥性，因授朝散大夫，賜几杖衣服。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Quan was one hundred three years old; Taizong visited his home, observed his food and drink, and inquired about the properties of medicines; he therefore granted him Grand Master for Palace Counsel and bestowed a couch, staff, and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Quan was one hundred and three. Taizong visited his home, watched him eat and drink, and questioned him about medicinal properties. He then granted Quan the title Grand Master for Palace Counsel and gave him a couch, staff, and robes.

sentences.zh: 其年卒。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 撰《脈經》、《針方》、《明堂人形圖》各一卷。

translations.literal: He compiled one fascicle each of Pulse Classic, Needle Formulas, and Bright Hall Human Figure Diagram.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote one fascicle each of Pulse Classic, Needle Formulas, and Bright Hall Human Figure Diagram.

sentences.zh: 弟 立言

translations.literal: Younger brother Liyan
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Liyan

sentences.zh: 弟立言，武德中累遷太常丞。

translations.literal: His younger brother Liyan, during Wude, was promoted in stages to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Liyan rose during the Wude era to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫杜淹患風毒發腫，太宗令立言視之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Du Yan suffered wind toxin with swelling outbreaks; Taizong ordered Liyan to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Du Yan suffered from wind toxin with painful swelling. Taizong ordered Liyan to examine him.

sentences.zh: 既而奏曰：「從今更十一日午時必死。」

translations.literal: He then reported: "From today, eleven days hence at the noon hour he will certainly die."
translations.idiomatic: He then reported: "Eleven days from now, at the noon hour, he will die."

sentences.zh: 果如其言。

translations.literal: It came about exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 時有尼明律，年六十余，患心腹鼓脹，身體嬴瘦，已經二年。

translations.literal: At the time there was the nun Minglü, over sixty years old, suffering from distension of heart and belly, her body emaciated and thin, already for two years.
translations.idiomatic: There was a nun named Minglü, over sixty, who had suffered for two years from abdominal distension and wasting emaciation.

sentences.zh: 立言診脈曰：「其腹內有蟲，當是誤食發為之耳。」

translations.literal: Liyan, taking the pulse, said: "Within her belly there are worms; this must be from mistakenly eating hair that became them."
translations.idiomatic: After taking her pulse, Liyan said: "There are worms in her belly—she must have eaten hair by mistake, and it has bred inside her."

sentences.zh: 因令服雄黃，須臾吐一蛇，如人手小指，唯無眼，燒之，猶有發氣，其疾乃愈。

translations.literal: He therefore had her take realgar; in a moment she vomited a snake like a human little finger, only without eyes; when burned it still had the smell of hair, and her illness was then cured.
translations.idiomatic: He had her take realgar, and presently she vomited a snake the size of a little finger, eyeless; when burned it still smelled of hair, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 立言尋卒。

translations.literal: Liyan soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Liyan died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 撰《本草音義》七卷，《古今錄驗方》五十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled seven fascicles of Materia Medica Phonetic Glosses and fifty fascicles of Recorded Efficacious Formulas Ancient and Modern.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote seven fascicles of Materia Medica Phonetic Glosses and fifty fascicles of Recorded Efficacious Formulas Ancient and Modern.

sentences.zh: 宋俠者，洺州清漳人，北齊東平王文學孝正之子也。

translations.literal: Song Xia was a man of Qingzhang in Mingzhou, son of Xiao Zheng, literary attendant to the Prince of Dongping of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xia was from Qingzhang in Mingzhou, the son of Xiao Zheng, literary attendant to the Prince of Dongping of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 亦以醫術著名。

translations.literal: He too was famed for medical skill.
translations.idiomatic: He too was renowned for his medical skill.

sentences.zh: 官至朝散大夫、藥藏監。

translations.literal: He reached office as Grand Master for Palace Counsel and superintendent of the pharmaceutical repository.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand master for palace counsel and superintendent of the pharmaceutical repository.

sentences.zh: 撰《經心錄》十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He compiled ten fascicles of Heart Classic Records, which circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ten fascicles of Heart Classic Records, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 許胤宗

translations.literal: Xu Yinzong
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yinzong

sentences.zh: 許胤宗，常州義興人也。

translations.literal: Xu Yinzong was a native of Yixing in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yinzong was a native of Yixing in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 初事陳，為新蔡王外兵參軍。

translations.literal: He first served Chen as external military staff officer to the Prince of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the Chen dynasty as external military staff officer to the Prince of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 時柳太后病風不言，名醫治皆不愈，脈益沉而噤。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Dowager Liu suffered wind ailment and could not speak; famous physicians treated her but none cured her; her pulse grew ever deeper and she was mute.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Liu suffered a wind disorder that left her unable to speak. Famous physicians could not cure her; her pulse grew weaker and she could not utter a word.

sentences.zh: 胤宗曰：「口不可下藥，宜以湯氣薰之。

translations.literal: Yinzong said: "Medicine cannot be taken by mouth; she should be fumigated with the vapor of a decoction.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzong said: "She cannot swallow medicine. She should be treated with the steam of a medicinal decoction.

sentences.zh: 令藥入腠理，周理即差。」

translations.literal: Let the medicine enter the interstices of the flesh; when it pervades the principles of the body, she will recover."
translations.idiomatic: Let the medicine enter through the pores; once it reaches every part of the body, she will recover."

sentences.zh: 乃造黃蓍防風湯數十斛，置於床下，氣如煙霧，其夜便得語。

translations.literal: He then prepared several tens of hu of astragalus and saposhnikovia decoction, placed it beneath the bed; the vapor was like mist, and that night she could speak.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared several tens of hu of an astragalus and saposhnikovia decoction and placed it beneath her bed. The steam rose like mist, and that night she could speak again.

sentences.zh: 由是超拜義興太守。

translations.literal: Because of this he was promoted out of turn to grand administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted out of turn to grand administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，曆尚藥奉禦。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he entered Sui and successively served as imperial attendant of the pharmaceutical office.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Chen he entered Sui service and became imperial attendant of the pharmaceutical office.

sentences.zh: 武德初，累授散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Early in Wude he was promoted in stages to Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era he was promoted to attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 時關中多骨蒸病，得之必死，遞相連染，諸醫無能療者。

translations.literal: At the time in Guanzhong there were many cases of bone-steaming disease; those who contracted it certainly died, infecting one another in succession, and no physician could treat it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bone-steaming fever was rampant in Guanzhong. Those who contracted it invariably died, and the disease spread from one person to the next; no physician could treat it.

sentences.zh: 胤宗每療，無不愈。

translations.literal: Whenever Yinzong treated it, none failed to recover.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yinzong treated it, the patient recovered.

sentences.zh: 或謂曰：「公醫術若神，何不著書以貽將來？」

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "Your medical skill is like a spirit's—why not write a book to bequeath to posterity?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him: "Your medical skill is almost supernatural—why not write a book for future generations?"

sentences.zh: 胤宗曰：「醫者，意也，在人思慮。

translations.literal: Yinzong said: 'Medicine is intention—it lies in a person's thinking.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzong replied: 'Medicine is a matter of insight—it depends on how one thinks.

sentences.zh: 又脈候幽微，苦其難別，意之所解，口莫能宣。

translations.literal: Moreover pulse signs are subtle and obscure, painfully hard to distinguish; what the mind comprehends, the mouth cannot declare.
translations.idiomatic: Pulse signs are subtle and hard to distinguish; what the mind grasps, the tongue cannot express.

sentences.zh: 且古之名手，唯是別脈；

translations.literal: Moreover the famous masters of old distinguished only the pulse;
translations.idiomatic: The great physicians of old distinguished pulses alone;

sentences.zh: 脈既精別，然後識病。

translations.literal: once the pulse was finely distinguished, only then did they recognize the disease.
translations.idiomatic: only after mastering the pulse could they recognize the disease.

sentences.zh: 夫病之於藥，有正相當者，唯須單用一味，直攻彼病，藥力既純，病即立愈。

translations.literal: As for the relation of disease to medicine, when there is a direct correspondence, one need only use a single ingredient alone, attacking that disease directly; once the drug's power is pure, the disease is immediately cured.
translations.idiomatic: When a disease matches a drug precisely, one need only use a single ingredient and strike directly at the illness. With the drug's power undiluted, the disease is cured at once.

sentences.zh: 今人不能別脈，莫識病源，以情臆度，多安藥味。

translations.literal: People today cannot distinguish pulses, do not know the source of disease, and by emotion and guesswork add many drug ingredients.
translations.idiomatic: Today's physicians cannot distinguish pulses or identify the source of disease. They guess by feeling and pile many ingredients into a prescription.

sentences.zh: 譬之於獵，未知兔所，多發人馬，空地遮圍，或冀一人偶然逢也。

translations.literal: It is like hunting: not knowing where the hare is, they send out many men and horses to encircle empty ground, perhaps hoping one man will happen to meet it.
translations.idiomatic: It is like hunting without knowing where the hare lies: one sends out many beaters to surround empty ground, hoping someone will stumble on the game by chance.

sentences.zh: 如此療疾，不亦疏乎！

translations.literal: To treat illness in this way—is it not crude!
translations.idiomatic: To treat illness this way—is that not reckless?

sentences.zh: 假令一藥偶然當病，復共他味相和，君臣相制，氣勢不行，所以難差，諒由於此。

translations.literal: Even if one drug by chance matches the disease, when it is again combined with other flavors, sovereign and minister counteract each other, the momentum does not proceed—hence recovery is hard; surely it is because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Even when one drug happens to match the disease, mixing it with others makes sovereign and minister ingredients counteract one another so the remedy's force cannot act—no doubt that is why cures are so hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 脈之深趣，既不可言，虛設經方，豈加於舊。

translations.literal: The deep subtleties of the pulse cannot be spoken; to set up canonical formulas in vain—how could they improve on the old?
translations.idiomatic: The deep art of pulse diagnosis cannot be put into words; composing formal prescriptions in vain could hardly improve on what the ancients knew.

sentences.zh: 吾思之久矣，故不能著述耳！」

translations.literal: I have pondered this for long, and therefore cannot compose a book!"
translations.idiomatic: I have thought about this for a long time, which is why I cannot write a book."

sentences.zh: 年九十餘卒。

translations.literal: At over ninety years of age he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at over ninety years of age.

sentences.zh: 乙弗弘禮

translations.literal: Yifu Hongli
translations.idiomatic: Yifu Hongli

sentences.zh: 乙弗弘禮，貝州高唐人也。

translations.literal: Yifu Hongli was a native of Gaotang in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu Hongli was a native of Gaotang in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝居籓，召令相己。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang of Sui was residing as prince, he summoned Hongli to physiognomize him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang of Sui was still a prince, he summoned Hongli to read his physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 弘禮跪而賀曰：「大王骨法非常，必為萬乘之主，誠願戒之在得。」

translations.literal: Hongli knelt and congratulated him, saying: "Your Highness's bone structure is extraordinary; you are destined to become lord of ten thousand chariots. I sincerely pray you guard against excess in attainment."
translations.idiomatic: Hongli knelt and congratulated him, saying: "Your Highness's bone structure is extraordinary—you are destined to rule the realm. I earnestly urge you to guard against excess once you attain it."

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，召天下道術人，置坊以居之，仍令弘禮統攝。

translations.literal: When Yang became emperor, he summoned masters of the Way and the arts from throughout the realm, established quarters for them to dwell in, and put Hongli in charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang took the throne, he summoned masters of the Way and the arts from across the realm, housed them in dedicated quarters, and placed Hongli in overall charge.

sentences.zh: 帝見海內漸亂，玄象錯謬，內懷憂恐，嘗謂弘禮曰：「卿昔相朕，其言已驗。

translations.literal: The emperor saw the realm gradually falling into disorder and celestial signs going awry; inwardly anxious and fearful, he once said to Hongli: 'You once physiognomized me, and your words have come true.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm slide into disorder and celestial signs turn ominous, the emperor grew inwardly fearful. He once told Hongli: 'You once read my physiognomy, and your words have already come true.

sentences.zh: 且占相道術，朕頗自知。

translations.literal: Moreover, in divination, physiognomy, and the arts of the Way, I know myself fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in divination, physiognomy, and the arts of the Way, I know my own art fairly well.

sentences.zh: 卿更相朕，終當何如？」

translations.literal: Physiognomize me again—what will my end be?"
translations.idiomatic: Read my physiognomy again—what will my end be?"

sentences.zh: 弘禮逡巡不敢答。

translations.literal: Hongli hesitated and dared not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Hongli hesitated and dared not answer.

sentences.zh: 帝迫曰：「卿言與朕術不同，罪當死。」

translations.literal: The emperor pressed him: "If your words differ from my art, the crime deserves death."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him: "If what you say differs from my own art, the offense deserves death."

sentences.zh: 弘禮曰：「臣本觀相書，凡人之相，有類于陛下者，不得善終。

translations.literal: Hongli said: 'Your servant originally studied physiognomy books. Ordinary men's features resembling Your Majesty's do not meet a good end.
translations.idiomatic: Hongli said: 'I studied physiognomy books. Ordinary men whose features resemble Your Majesty's do not meet a good end.

sentences.zh: 臣聞聖人不相，故知凡聖不同耳。」

translations.literal: I have heard that sages are not physiognomized, and therefore know that the ordinary and the sacred differ.'
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that sages are not read by physiognomy, and so I know that the ordinary and the sacred are not the same.'

sentences.zh: 自是帝嘗遣使監之，不得與人交言。

translations.literal: From then on the emperor often sent agents to watch him, and he was not permitted to converse with others.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor often sent agents to watch him, and he was forbidden to speak with others.

sentences.zh: 初，泗州刺史薛大鼎隋時嘗坐事沒為奴，貞觀初，與數人詣之，大鼎次至，弘禮曰：「君奴也，欲何所相？」

translations.literal: Earlier, Xue Dading, regional inspector of Si, had during Sui been reduced to servitude for an offense. Early in Zhenguan he came with several others to see Hongli; when Dading's turn came, Hongli said: "You are a slave—what do you wish physiognomized?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xue Dading, regional inspector of Si, had been enslaved during Sui for an offense. Early in the Zhenguan era he came with several others to see Hongli. When Dading's turn came, Hongli said: "You are a slave—what is there to read?"

sentences.zh: 咸曰：「何以知之？」

translations.literal: They all said: 'How do you know?'
translations.idiomatic: They all asked: 'How do you know?'

sentences.zh: 弘禮曰：「觀其頭目，直是賤人，但不知餘處何如耳？」

translations.literal: Hongli said: 'Looking at his head and eyes, he is plainly a base man—but I do not know how the rest of him fares.'
translations.idiomatic: Hongli said: 'Judging by his head and eyes, he is plainly a man of low station—but I cannot tell how the rest of him will fare.'

sentences.zh: 大鼎有慚色，乃解衣視之，弘禮曰：「看君面，不異前言。

translations.literal: Dading looked ashamed; he removed his clothing for inspection. Hongli said: 'Examining your face, it does not differ from what I said before.
translations.idiomatic: Dading flushed with shame, then stripped so Hongli could examine him further. Hongli said: 'Your face confirms what I said before.

sentences.zh: 占君自腰已下，當為方岳之任。」

translations.literal: Reading you from the waist downward, you are destined for the office of regional governor.'
translations.idiomatic: From the waist down, you are destined for a regional governor's post.'

sentences.zh: 其占相皆此類也。

translations.literal: His physiognomic readings were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His physiognomic readings were mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末卒。

translations.literal: He died at the end of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the end of the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 袁天綱

translations.literal: Yuan Tiangang
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tiangang

sentences.zh: 袁天綱，益州成都人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Tiangang was a native of Chengdu in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tiangang was a native of Chengdu in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 尤工相術。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，為資官令。

translations.literal: During Daye of Sui he served as director of the granary office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era of Sui he served as director of the granary office.

sentences.zh: 武德初，蜀道使詹俊赤牒授火井令。

translations.literal: Early in Wude, the Shu circuit envoy Zhan Jun personally delivered a warrant appointing him magistrate of Huojing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era, the Shu circuit envoy Zhan Jun personally delivered an appointment warrant making him magistrate of Huojing.

sentences.zh: 初，天綱以大業元年至洛陽。

translations.literal: At first, Tiangang arrived in Luoyang in the first year of Daye.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang first arrived in Luoyang in the first year of Daye.

sentences.zh: 時杜淹、王珪、韋挺就之相。

translations.literal: At the time Du Yan, Wang Gui, and Wei Ting came to him for physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Du Yan, Wang Gui, and Wei Ting came to him to have their physiognomy read.

sentences.zh: 天綱謂淹曰：「公蘭台成就，學堂寬博，必得親糾察之官，以文藻見知。」

translations.literal: Tiangang told Yan: "Your orchid terrace is complete, your study hall broad—you will surely obtain an office of close scrutiny, distinguished for literary talent."
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang told Yan: "Your orchid terrace is complete and your study hall broad—you will surely obtain a post of close scrutiny and be known for literary talent."

sentences.zh: 謂王曰：「公三亭成就，天地相臨，從今十年已外，必得五品要職。」

translations.literal: He told Wang: 'Your three pavilions are complete, heaven and earth facing each other—from ten years hence you will surely obtain a major post of the fifth rank.'
translations.idiomatic: He told Wang: 'Your three pavilions are complete and heaven and earth face each other—from ten years on you will surely obtain an important fifth-rank post.'

sentences.zh: 謂韋曰：「公面似大獸之面，交友極誠，必得士友攜接，初為武職。」

translations.literal: He told Wei: 'Your face resembles the face of a great beast; in friendship you are utterly sincere—you will surely be taken up by scholarly friends, and at first hold a military post.'
translations.idiomatic: He told Wei: 'Your face resembles that of a great beast; in friendship you are utterly sincere—you will surely be taken up by men of talent, and at first hold a military post.'

sentences.zh: 復謂淹等「二十年外，終恐三賢同被責黜，暫去即還。」

translations.literal: He further told Yan and the others: 'Beyond twenty years, I fear you three worthies will together suffer censure and dismissal, but after departing you will return.'
translations.idiomatic: He further told Yan and the others: 'Beyond twenty years, I fear you three worthies will together be censured and dismissed, but after a temporary departure you will return.'

sentences.zh: 淹尋遷侍御史，武德中為天策府兵曹、文學館學士。

translations.literal: Yan was soon promoted to attendant censor; during Wude he served as military staff officer of the Heavenly Stratagem headquarters and academician of the Literary Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was soon promoted to attendant censor; during the Wude era he served as military staff officer of the Heavenly Stratagem headquarters and as an academician of the Literary Hall.

sentences.zh: 王珪為太子中允。

translations.literal: Wang Gui served as attendant to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui served as attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 韋挺，隋末與隱太子友善，後太子引以為率。

translations.literal: Wei Ting, at the end of Sui, was friendly with the Hidden Crown Prince; later the prince brought him in as leader of his guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ting, at the end of Sui, was friendly with the Hidden Crown Prince; later the prince brought him in as commander of his guard.

sentences.zh: 至武德六年，俱配流巂州。

translations.literal: By the sixth year of Wude all were banished to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth year of the Wude era all were banished to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 淹等至益州，見天綱曰：「袁公洛邑之言，則信矣。

translations.literal: When Yan and the others reached Yizhou, they saw Tiangang and said: 'Master Yuan, your words about Luoyang have proved true.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan and the others reached Yizhou, they visited Tiangang and said: 'Master Yuan, your words about Luoyang have proved true.

sentences.zh: 未知今日之後何如？」

translations.literal: We do not know what will happen from today onward?"
translations.idiomatic: We do not know what will happen from today onward?"

sentences.zh: 天綱曰：「公等骨法，大勝往時，終當俱受榮貴。」

translations.literal: Tiangang said: 'Your bone structures far surpass those of before; in the end you will all receive honor and high rank.'
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang said: 'Your bone structures far surpass what they were before; in the end you will all receive honor and high rank.'

sentences.zh: 至九年，被召入京，共造天綱。

translations.literal: By the ninth year they were summoned to the capital and together visited Tiangang.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth year they were summoned to the capital and together visited Tiangang.

sentences.zh: 天綱謂杜公曰：「即當得三品要職，年壽非天綱所知。

translations.literal: Tiangang told Master Du: 'You will shortly obtain a major post of the third rank; length of life is not something Tiangang can know.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang told Master Du: 'You will shortly obtain an important third-rank post; as for length of life, that is not something Tiangang can know.

sentences.zh: 王、韋二公，在後當得三品官，兼有年壽，然晚途皆不稱愜，韋公尤甚。」

translations.literal: The two gentlemen Wang and Wei will later obtain third-rank offices and also have length of years, yet in their later course none will be content—Master Wei especially so."
translations.idiomatic: The two gentlemen Wang and Wei will later obtain third-rank offices and also enjoy long life, yet none of you will be content in your later years—Master Wei especially so."

sentences.zh: 淹至京，拜御史大夫、檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Yan reached the capital and was appointed censor-in-chief and acting minister of the personnel department.
translations.idiomatic: Yan reached the capital and was appointed censor-in-chief and acting minister of the personnel department.

sentences.zh: 王珪尋授侍中，出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Gui was soon appointed palace attendant and sent out as prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui was soon appointed palace attendant and then sent out as prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 韋挺曆御史大夫、太常卿，貶象州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei Ting successively served as censor-in-chief and minister of imperial sacrifices, then was demoted to prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ting served successively as censor-in-chief and minister of imperial sacrifices, then was demoted to prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 皆如天綱之言。

translations.literal: All came about as Tiangang had said.
translations.idiomatic: All came about exactly as Tiangang had said.

sentences.zh: 大業末，竇軌客游德陽，嘗問天綱。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, Dou Gui, traveling as a guest in Deyang, once questioned Tiangang.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era, Dou Gui, traveling as a guest in Deyang, once consulted Tiangang.

sentences.zh: 天綱謂曰：「君額上伏犀貫玉枕，輔角又成、必于梁、益州大樹功業。」

translations.literal: Tiangang told him: "On your forehead the hidden rhinoceros pierces the jade pillow, and your auxiliary angles are complete—you will surely establish great achievements in Liang and Yizhou."
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang told him: "On your forehead the hidden rhinoceros pierces the jade pillow, and your auxiliary angles are complete—you will surely establish great achievements in Liang and Yizhou."

sentences.zh: 武德初，軌為益州行台僕射，引天綱，深禮之。

translations.literal: Early in Wude, Gui was vice director of the Yizhou field headquarters; he brought in Tiangang and treated him with deep courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era, Gui served as vice director of the Yizhou field headquarters; he brought in Tiangang and treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 天綱又謂軌曰：「骨法成就，不異往時之言。

translations.literal: Tiangang again told Gui: 'Your bone structure is complete—no different from what I said before.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang again told Gui: 'Your bone structure is complete—just as I said before.

sentences.zh: 然目氣赤脈貫瞳子，語則赤氣浮面。

translations.literal: Yet the qi of your eyes is red, crimson vessels pierce the pupils, and when you speak red qi floats upon your face.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the qi of your eyes is red, crimson vessels pierce the pupils, and when you speak a red flush rises to your face.

sentences.zh: 如為將軍，恐多殺人。

translations.literal: If you become a general, I fear you will kill many.
translations.idiomatic: If you become a general, I fear you will kill many people.

sentences.zh: 願深自誡慎。」

translations.literal: I pray you deeply guard and restrain yourself."
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to restrain yourself deeply."

sentences.zh: 武德九年，軌坐事被征，將赴京，謂天綱曰：「更得何官？」

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wude, Gui was implicated in an affair and summoned; about to go to the capital, he asked Tiangang: 'What office will I receive next?'
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Wude era, Gui was implicated in an affair and summoned to the capital. About to depart, he asked Tiangang: 'What office will I receive next?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「面上家人坐仍未見動，輔角右畔光澤，更有喜色，至京必承恩，還來此任。」

translations.literal: He said: 'The family-seat on your face has not yet moved; the right side of your auxiliary angle is lustrous, with further color of joy—you will surely receive grace at the capital and return to this post.'
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'The family-seat on your face has not yet shifted; the right side of your auxiliary angle is lustrous and shows further signs of joy—you will surely receive imperial favor at the capital and return to this post.'

sentences.zh: 其年果重授益州都督。

translations.literal: That year he was indeed reappointed military commissioner of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was indeed reappointed military commissioner of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 則天初在繈褓，天綱來至第中，謂其母曰：「唯夫人骨法，必生貴子。」

translations.literal: When Zetian was still in swaddling clothes, Tiangang came to the household and told her mother: "By your bone structure alone, you will surely bear a noble child."
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian was still in swaddling clothes, Tiangang came to the household and told her mother: "By your bone structure alone, you will surely bear a noble child."

sentences.zh: 乃召諸子，令天綱相之。

translations.literal: He then summoned the sons and had Tiangang physiognomize them.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the sons and had Tiangang read their physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 見元慶、元爽曰：「此二子皆保家之主，官可至三品。」

translations.literal: Seeing Yuangqing and Yuanshuang, he said: "These two sons will both be masters who preserve the household; their offices may reach the third rank."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Yuangqing and Yuanshuang, he said: "These two sons will both be pillars of the household; their offices may reach the third rank."

sentences.zh: 見韓國夫人曰：「此女亦大貴，然不利其夫。」

translations.literal: Seeing the Lady of Han, he said: 'This girl is also greatly noble, yet it will not benefit her husband.'
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Lady of Han, he said: 'This girl is also greatly noble, yet it will not benefit her husband.'

sentences.zh: 乳母時抱則天，衣男子之服，天綱曰：「此郎君子神色爽徹，不可易知，試令行看。」

translations.literal: The wet nurse was holding Zetian, dressed in boy's clothing. Tiangang said: 'This young gentleman's spirit and color are clear and bright—not easily known; try having him walk and look.'
translations.idiomatic: The wet nurse was holding Wu Zetian, dressed in boy's clothing. Tiangang said: 'This young gentleman's spirit and color are clear and bright—not easily read; try having him walk and look around.'

sentences.zh: 於是步於床前，仍令舉目，天綱大驚曰：「此郎君子龍睛鳳頸，貴人之極也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he walked before the bed and was made to lift his eyes. Tiangang cried out in astonishment: 'This young gentleman has dragon eyes and phoenix neck—the utmost of nobility.'
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the child walked before the bed and was made to lift his eyes. Tiangang cried out in astonishment: 'This young gentleman has dragon eyes and a phoenix neck—the utmost of nobility.'

sentences.zh: 更轉側視之，又驚曰：「必若是女，實不可窺測，後當為天下之主矣！」

translations.literal: Turning to view from the side, he was astonished again: 'If this must be a girl, it truly cannot be fathomed—later she will become sovereign of the realm!'
translations.idiomatic: Turning to view the child from the side, he was astonished again: 'If this must be a girl, she truly cannot be fathomed—later she will become sovereign of the realm!'

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年，太宗聞其名，召至九成宮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan, Taizong heard his name and summoned him to Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Zhenguan era, Taizong heard his name and summoned him to Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人岑文本令視之。

translations.literal: At the time Secretariat drafter Cen Wenben had him examine him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Secretariat drafter Cen Wenben had him read his physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 天綱曰：「舍人學堂成就，眉覆過目，文才振於海內，頭又生骨，猶未大成，若得三品，恐是損壽之征。」

translations.literal: Tiangang said: "Drafter, your study hall is complete, your brows cover past the eyes, your literary talent resounds within the seas, and bone has grown on your head—yet it is not fully mature; if you obtain the third rank, I fear it is a sign of shortened life."
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang said: "Drafter, your study hall is complete, your brows cover past the eyes, your literary talent resounds throughout the realm, and bone has grown on your head—yet it is not fully mature; if you reach the third rank, I fear it is a sign of shortened life."

sentences.zh: 文本官至中書令，尋卒。

translations.literal: Wenben reached the post of chief minister of the Secretariat and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben rose to chief minister of the Secretariat and soon died.

sentences.zh: 其年，侍御史張行成、馬周同問天綱，天綱曰：「馬侍御伏犀貫腦，兼有玉枕，又背如負物，當富貴不可言。

translations.literal: That year attending censor Zhang Xingcheng and Ma Zhou together questioned Tiangang. Tiangang said: 'Attending censor Ma, your hidden rhinoceros pierces the brain and you also have the jade pillow; your back is as if bearing a burden—you will be rich and noble beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: That year attending censor Zhang Xingcheng and Ma Zhou together consulted Tiangang. Tiangang said: 'Attending censor Ma, your hidden rhinoceros pierces the brain and you also have the jade pillow; your back is as if bearing a burden—you will be rich and noble beyond words.

sentences.zh: 近古已來，君臣道合，罕有如公者。

translations.literal: Since near antiquity, the harmony of lord and minister has rarely been like yours.
translations.idiomatic: Since recent antiquity, the harmony of lord and minister has rarely been like yours.

sentences.zh: 公面色赤，命門色暗，耳後骨不起，耳無根，只恐非壽者。」

translations.literal: Your facial color is red, the life-gate color is dark, the bone behind the ears does not rise, the ears have no root—I fear only that you are not long-lived."
translations.idiomatic: Your facial color is red, the life-gate color is dark, the bone behind the ears does not rise, and the ears have no root—I fear only that you are not long-lived."

sentences.zh: 周後位至中書令、兼吏部尚書，年四十八卒。

translations.literal: Zhou later reached chief minister of the Secretariat and concurrent minister of the personnel department; he died at forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou later rose to chief minister of the Secretariat and concurrent minister of the personnel department; he died at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 謂行成曰：「公五嶽四瀆成就，下亭豐滿，得官雖晚，終居宰輔之地。」

translations.literal: He told Xingcheng: "Your five peaks and four waterways are complete, your lower pavilion full—though your office comes late, in the end you will occupy the seat of chief counselor."
translations.idiomatic: He told Xingcheng: "Your five peaks and four waterways are complete, your lower pavilion full—though your office comes late, in the end you will occupy the seat of chief counselor."

sentences.zh: 行成後至尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Xingcheng later reached Vice Director of the Right of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xingcheng later rose to vice director of the right of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天綱相人所中，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Tiangang's physiognomic hits on people were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang's physiognomic readings proved accurate in cases like these.

sentences.zh: 申國公高士廉嘗謂曰：「君更作何官？」

translations.literal: Duke of Shen State Gao Shilian once asked him: "What office will you hold next?"
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Shen Gao Shilian once asked him: "What office will you hold next?"

sentences.zh: 天綱曰：「自知相命，今年四月盡矣。」

translations.literal: Tiangang said: 'Knowing my own fate in physiognomy, this year ends in the fourth month.'
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang said: 'Knowing my own fate from physiognomy, my life ends in the fourth month of this year.'

sentences.zh: 果至是月而卒。

translations.literal: Indeed, in that month he died.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, he died in that month.

sentences.zh: 孫思邈

translations.literal: Sun Simiao
translations.idiomatic: Sun Simiao

sentences.zh: 孫思邈，京兆華原人也。

translations.literal: Sun Simiao was a native of Huayuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Simiao was a native of Huayuan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 七歲就學，日誦千餘言。

translations.literal: At seven he began study, reciting over a thousand words a day.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he began his studies, reciting over a thousand words a day.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，善談莊、老及百家之說，兼好釋典。

translations.literal: At his capping he was skilled at discussing Zhuangzi, Laozi, and the teachings of the hundred schools, and also loved Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: At his coming of age he was skilled at discussing Zhuangzi, Laozi, and the teachings of the hundred schools, and also loved Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 洛州總管獨孤信見而歎曰：「此聖童也。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin, regional commander of Luozhou, saw him and sighed: "This is a sage child.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin, regional commander of Luozhou, saw him and sighed: "This is a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 但恨其器大，難為用也。」

translations.literal: Only I regret that his vessel is too great—hard to put to use."
translations.idiomatic: Only I regret that his capacity is too great—hard to put to ordinary use."

sentences.zh: 周宣帝時，思邈以王室多故，隱居太白山。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xuan of Zhou, Simiao, because the royal house had many troubles, withdrew to Mount Taibai.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Xuan of Zhou, Simiao withdrew to Mount Taibai because the royal house was beset by troubles.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝輔政，征為國子博士，稱疾不起。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent, he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy but pleaded illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent, Simiao was summoned as erudite of the Imperial Academy but pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂所親曰：「過五十年，當有聖人出，吾方助之以濟人。」

translations.literal: He once told those close to him: "After fifty years a sage will appear, and only then will I assist him in saving people."
translations.idiomatic: He once told those close to him: "In fifty years a sage will appear, and only then will I assist him in healing people."

sentences.zh: 及太宗即位，召詣京師，嗟其容色甚少，謂曰：「故知有道者誠可尊重，羨門、廣成，豈虛言哉！」

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was summoned to the capital; the emperor marvelled at how youthful he still looked and said: 'Thus one knows that a man of the Way is truly worthy of respect—what Xianmen and Guangcheng said was no empty talk!'
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Simiao was summoned to the capital. The emperor marvelled at how youthful he still looked and said: 'Thus one knows that a man of the Way is truly worthy of respect—what Xianmen and Guangcheng said was no empty talk!'

sentences.zh: 將授以爵位，固辭不受。

translations.literal: He was about to be granted a noble rank, but firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to grant him a noble rank, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 顯慶四年，高宗召見，拜諫議大夫，又固辭不受。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianqing, Gaozong summoned him and appointed him Remonstrating Grand Master, but again he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianqing, Gaozong summoned him and appointed him remonstrating grand master, but again he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，辭疾請歸，特賜良馬，及鄱陽公主邑司以居焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, he pleaded illness and requested to return home. A fine horse was specially bestowed on him, and the revenue office of Princess Poyang was given for him to reside in.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan, he pleaded illness and asked to return home. A fine horse was specially bestowed on him, and he was given the revenue office of Princess Poyang as a residence.

sentences.zh: 當時知名之士宋令文、孟詵、盧照鄰等，執師資之禮以事焉。

translations.literal: At the time, noted men such as Song Lingwen, Meng Shen, and Lu Zhaolin served him with the rites of a teacher and pupil.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, noted men such as Song Lingwen, Meng Shen, and Lu Zhaolin treated him with the deference due from pupils to a teacher.

sentences.zh: 思邈嘗從幸九成宮，照鄰留在其宅。

translations.literal: Simiao once followed the imperial progress to Jiucheng Palace, and Zhaolin remained at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Simiao once followed the imperial progress to Jiucheng Palace, Lu Zhaolin stayed behind at his residence.

sentences.zh: 時庭前有病梨樹，照鄰為之賦，其序曰：「癸酉之歲，余臥疾長安光德坊之官舍。

translations.literal: At the time, there was a diseased pear tree before the courtyard, and Zhaolin composed a fu about it. Its preface said: "In the guiyou year, I lay ill in official lodgings in Guangde Ward in Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, there was a diseased pear tree in front of the courtyard, and Lu Zhaolin composed a fu on it. Its preface said: "In the guiyou year, I lay ill in official lodgings in Guangde Ward in Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 父老云：『是鄱陽公主邑司。

translations.literal: The elders said: 'This is the revenue office of Princess Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: The elders said: 'This is the revenue office of Princess Poyang.

sentences.zh: 昔公主未嫁而卒，故其邑廢。』

translations.literal: In the past, the princess died before marrying, and therefore her revenue establishment was left vacant.'
translations.idiomatic: In the past, the princess died before marrying, so her revenue establishment was left vacant.'

sentences.zh: 時有孫思邈處士居之。

translations.literal: At this time the retired scholar Sun Simiao resided there.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the retired scholar Sun Simiao was living there.

sentences.zh: 邈道合古今，學殫數術。

translations.literal: Simiao’s Way accorded with past and present, and his learning exhausted the arts of calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Simiao’s Way accorded with past and present, and his learning exhausted the arts of numbers and techniques.

sentences.zh: 高談正一，則古之蒙莊子；深入不二，則今之維摩詰。

translations.literal: In lofty discourse on the Orthodox Unity, he was the Meng Zhuangzi of old; in penetrating the nondual, he was the Vimalakirti of today.
translations.idiomatic: In lofty discourse on the Orthodox Unity, he was like the ancient Meng Zhuangzi; in penetrating the nondual, he was the Vimalakirti of the present age.

sentences.zh: 其推步甲乙，度量乾坤，則洛下閎、安期先生之儔也。」

translations.literal: As for his calculations of the jia and yi and his measuring of heaven and earth, he was a peer of Luo Xiahong and Master Anqi."
translations.idiomatic: As for his calendrical calculations and his measuring of heaven and earth, he was a peer of Luo Xiahong and Master Anqi."

sentences.zh: 照鄰有惡疾，醫所不能愈，乃問思邈：「名醫愈疾，其道何如？」

translations.literal: Zhaolin had a severe illness that physicians could not cure, so he asked Simiao: "When famous physicians cure illness, what is their Way like?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhaolin had a severe illness that physicians could not cure, so he asked Simiao: "When eminent physicians cure illness, what is their Way like?"

sentences.zh: 思邈曰：「吾聞善言天者，必質之於人，善言人者，亦本之於天。

translations.literal: Simiao said: "I have heard that one who speaks well of heaven must test it against man, and one who speaks well of man must also root it in heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Simiao said: "I have heard that one who speaks well of heaven must test it against man, and one who speaks well of man must also root it in heaven.

sentences.zh: 天有四時五行，寒暑迭代，其轉運也，和而為雨，怒而為風，凝而為霜雪，張而為虹蜺，此天地之常數也。

translations.literal: Heaven has the four seasons and five phases, cold and heat succeeding each other; in its turning, harmony becomes rain, anger becomes wind, congealing becomes frost and snow, stretching becomes rainbow—this is the constant measure of heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has the four seasons and five phases, cold and heat succeeding each other; in its turning, harmony becomes rain, anger becomes wind, congealing becomes frost and snow, and stretching becomes rainbow—this is the constant measure of heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 人有四支五藏，一覺一寢，呼吸吐納，精氣往來，流而為榮衛，彰而為氣色，發而為音聲，此人之常數也。

translations.literal: Man has four limbs and five viscera, waking and sleeping, breathing in and out, essential qi coming and going; flowing it becomes nutritive and defensive qi, manifesting it becomes complexion, issuing it becomes voice—this is the constant measure of man.
translations.idiomatic: Man has four limbs and five viscera, waking and sleeping, breathing in and out, essential qi coming and going; flowing it becomes nutritive and defensive qi, manifesting it becomes complexion, and issuing it becomes voice—this is the constant measure of man.

sentences.zh: 陽用其形，陰用其精，天人之所同也。

translations.literal: Yang employs form, yin employs essence—this is what heaven and man share.
translations.idiomatic: Yang employs form, yin employs essence—this is what heaven and man share.

sentences.zh: 及其失也，蒸則生熱，否則生寒，結而為瘤贅，陷而為癰疽，奔而為喘乏，竭而為焦枯，診發乎面，變動乎形。

translations.literal: When this is lost, steaming produces heat, blockage produces cold, congealing becomes tumors and excrescences, sinking becomes abscesses and sores, racing becomes panting and exhaustion, depletion becomes withering desiccation—diagnosis appears on the face, change shows in the form.
translations.idiomatic: When this balance is lost, steaming produces heat and blockage produces cold; congealing becomes tumors and excrescences, sinking becomes abscesses and sores, racing becomes panting and exhaustion, and depletion becomes withering desiccation—diagnosis appears on the face and change shows in the body.

sentences.zh: 推此以及天地亦如之。

translations.literal: Extend this to heaven and earth and it is likewise so.
translations.idiomatic: Extend this principle to heaven and earth and it is likewise so.

sentences.zh: 故五緯盈縮，星辰錯行，日月薄蝕，孛彗飛流，此天地之危診也。

translations.literal: Thus the expansion and contraction of the five planets, the errant movement of stars, the eclipse of sun and moon, comets and shooting stars—these are the critical diagnoses of heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the expansion and contraction of the five planets, the errant movement of stars, eclipses of sun and moon, and comets and shooting stars—these are the critical diagnoses of heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 寒暑不時，天地之蒸否也；

translations.literal: Cold and heat out of season is the steaming and blockage of heaven and earth;
translations.idiomatic: Cold and heat out of season are the steaming and blockage of heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 石立土踴，天地之瘤贅也；

translations.literal: Stones standing up and earth leaping are the tumors and excrescences of heaven and earth;
translations.idiomatic: Stones standing upright and earth heaving upward are the tumors and excrescences of heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 山崩土陷，天地之癰疽也；

translations.literal: Mountain collapse and earth sinking are the carbuncles and sores of heaven and earth;
translations.idiomatic: Mountain collapses and earth sinks are the abscesses and sores of heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 奔風暴雨，天地之喘乏也；

translations.literal: Racing wind and rushing rain are the panting and exhaustion of heaven and earth;
translations.idiomatic: Gale winds and torrential rain are the panting and exhaustion of heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 川瀆竭涸，天地之焦枯也，良醫導之以藥石，救之以針劑，聖人和之以至德，輔之以人事，故形體有可愈之疾，天地有可消之災。」

translations.literal: Rivers and waterways running dry are the withering desiccation of heaven and earth. Good physicians guide the body with medicines and stones and rescue it with needles and decoctions; sages harmonize the world with supreme virtue and assist it with human affairs. Thus the body has illnesses that can be cured, and heaven and earth have calamities that can be dispelled."
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and waterways running dry are the withering desiccation of heaven and earth. Good physicians guide the body with medicines and stones and rescue it with needles and decoctions; sages harmonize the world with supreme virtue and assist it with human affairs. Thus the body has illnesses that can be cured, and heaven and earth have calamities that can be dispelled."

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 膽欲大而心欲小，智欲圓而行欲方。

translations.literal: The gall bladder should be large and the heart small; wisdom should be round and conduct square.
translations.idiomatic: One should wish for a large gall bladder and a small heart, round wisdom and square conduct.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「如臨深淵，如履薄冰」，謂小心也；

translations.literal: The Book of Odes says: "As if facing a deep abyss, as if treading on thin ice"—this speaks of caution;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "As if facing a deep abyss, as if treading on thin ice"—this speaks of caution;

sentences.zh: 「糾糾武夫，公侯干城」，謂大膽也。

translations.literal: "Sturdy warriors, bulwarks for lords and marquises"—this speaks of boldness.
translations.idiomatic: "Sturdy warriors, bulwarks for lords and marquises"—this speaks of boldness.

sentences.zh: 「不為利回，不為義疚」，行之方也；

translations.literal: "Not swayed by profit, not shamed by righteousness"—this is squareness in conduct;
translations.idiomatic: "Not swayed by profit, not shamed by righteousness"—this is squareness in conduct;

sentences.zh: 「見機而作，不俟終日」，智之圓也。

translations.literal: "Seeing the moment and acting, not waiting for the whole day"—this is roundness in wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: "Seeing the moment and acting, not waiting for the whole day"—this is roundness in wisdom.

sentences.zh: 思邈自云開皇辛酉歲生，至今年九十三矣；

translations.literal: Simiao himself said he was born in the xinyou year of the Kaihuang era, and by this year he was ninety-three;
translations.idiomatic: Simiao himself said he was born in the xinyou year of the Kaihuang era, and by this year he was ninety-three;

sentences.zh: 詢之鄉里，咸云數百歲人。

translations.literal: When asked in his home village, all said he was a man of several hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: When asked in his home village, all said he was a man of several hundred years.

sentences.zh: 話周、齊間事，歷歷如眼見。

translations.literal: Speaking of affairs between Zhou and Qi, he recounted them vividly as if he had seen them with his own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke of affairs between Northern Zhou and Northern Qi, he recounted them vividly, as if he had seen them with his own eyes.

sentences.zh: 以此參之，不啻百歲人矣。

translations.literal: Comparing by this, he was no less than a man of a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by this, he was surely no less than a man of a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 然猶視聽不衰，神采甚茂，可謂古之聰明博達不死者也。

translations.literal: Yet his sight and hearing had not declined, and his spirit was very vigorous—he could be called an undying man of ancient wisdom, erudition, and broad attainment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his sight and hearing had not declined, and his spirit was very vigorous—he could be called an undying man of ancient wisdom, erudition, and broad attainment.

sentences.zh: 初，魏徵等受詔修齊、梁、陳、周、隋五代史，恐有遺漏，屢訪之，思邈口以傳授，有如目睹。

translations.literal: Initially, when Wei Zheng and others received orders to compile the histories of the five dynasties Qi, Liang, Chen, Zhou, and Sui, fearing omissions they repeatedly consulted him; Simiao transmitted by word of mouth as if he had witnessed events himself.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Wei Zheng and others received orders to compile the histories of Qi, Liang, Chen, Zhou, and Sui, fearing omissions they repeatedly consulted him; Simiao transmitted accounts by word of mouth, as if he had witnessed the events himself.

sentences.zh: 東台侍郎孫處約將其五子侹、儆、俊、佑、佺以謁思邈，思邈曰：「俊當先貴；

translations.literal: East Terrace Vice Director Sun Chuyue brought his five sons Ting, Jing, Jun, You, and Quan to visit Simiao. Simiao said: "Jun will attain eminence first;
translations.idiomatic: East Terrace Vice Director Sun Chuyue brought his five sons Ting, Jing, Jun, You, and Quan to visit Simiao. Simiao said, "Jun will attain eminence first;

sentences.zh: 佑當晚達；

translations.literal: You will achieve distinction late;
translations.idiomatic: You will achieve distinction late;

sentences.zh: 佺最名重，禍在執兵。」

translations.literal: Quan will be most famed and honored, but disaster lies in wielding arms."
translations.idiomatic: Quan will be most famed and honored, but disaster lies in wielding arms."

sentences.zh: 後皆如其言。

translations.literal: Later all came to pass as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Later all came to pass as he had said.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事盧齊卿童幼時，請問人倫之事，思邈曰：「汝後五十年位登方伯，吾孫當為屬吏，可自保也。」

translations.literal: When Lu Qiqing, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was still a child, he asked about human relations. Simiao said: "Fifty years from now you will rise to the rank of regional inspector; my grandson will serve as your subordinate official—you may rely on this for your own protection."
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qiqing, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was still a child, he asked about human relations. Simiao said: "Fifty years from now you will rise to the rank of regional inspector; my grandson will serve as your subordinate official—you may rely on this for your own protection."

sentences.zh: 後齊卿為徐州刺史，思邈孫溥果為徐州蕭縣丞。

translations.literal: Later Qiqing became prefect of Xuzhou, and Simiao's grandson Pu indeed became assistant magistrate of Xiao County in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qiqing became prefect of Xuzhou, and Simiao's grandson Pu indeed became assistant magistrate of Xiao County in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 思邈初謂齊卿之時，溥猶未生，而預知其事。

translations.literal: When Simiao first spoke to Qiqing, Pu had not yet been born, yet he foreknew this matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Simiao first spoke to Qiqing, Pu had not yet been born, yet he foreknew this matter.

sentences.zh: 凡諸異跡，多此類也。

translations.literal: Of all such extraordinary signs, most were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Of all such extraordinary signs, most were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yongchun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Yongchun era.

sentences.zh: 遺令薄葬，不藏冥器，祭祀無牲牢。

translations.literal: His final instructions ordered a simple burial, no grave goods, and sacrifices without livestock.
translations.idiomatic: His final instructions ordered a simple burial, no grave goods, and sacrifices without livestock.

sentences.zh: 經月余，顏貌不改，舉屍就木，猶若空衣，時人異之。

translations.literal: After more than a month his countenance did not change; when the corpse was lifted into the coffin it was as if empty clothing—people of the time marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month his countenance did not change; when the corpse was lifted into the coffin it was as if empty clothing, and people of the time marveled at this.

sentences.zh: 自注《老子》、《莊子》，撰《千金方》三十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He annotated the Laozi and Zhuangzi himself, and compiled Prescriptions Worth a Thousand in Gold in thirty scrolls, which circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the Laozi and Zhuangzi himself, and compiled Prescriptions Worth a Thousand in Gold in thirty scrolls, which circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 又撰《福祿論》三卷，《攝生真錄》及《枕中素書》、《會三教論》各一卷。

translations.literal: He also wrote Treatise on Fortune and Blessings in three scrolls, and Records of True Nourishment of Life, Plain Book from the Pillow, and Discourse on Harmonizing the Three Teachings, each in one scroll.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Treatise on Fortune and Blessings in three scrolls, and Records of True Nourishment of Life, Plain Book from the Pillow, and Discourse on Harmonizing the Three Teachings, each in one scroll.

sentences.zh: 子行，天授中為鳳閣侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Xing served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion during the Tianshou era.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xing served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion during the Tianshou era.

sentences.zh: 明崇儼

translations.literal: Ming Chongyan
translations.idiomatic: Ming Chongyan

sentences.zh: 明崇儼，洛州偃師人。

translations.literal: Ming Chongyan was a native of Yanshi in Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Chongyan was a native of Yanshi in Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 其先平原士族，世仕江左。

translations.literal: His ancestors were a gentry clan of Pingyuan who for generations served in the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were a gentry clan of Pingyuan who for generations served in the lands south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 父恪，豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ke was prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ke was prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇儼年少時，隨父任安喜令，父之小吏有善役召鬼神者，崇儼盡能傳其術。

translations.literal: When Chongyan was young he accompanied his father to his post as magistrate of Anxi; among his father's minor clerks was one skilled at summoning spirits and ghosts, and Chongyan fully inherited his arts.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyan was young he accompanied his father to his post as magistrate of Anxi; among his father's minor clerks was one skilled at summoning spirits and ghosts, and Chongyan fully inherited his arts.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，應封嶽舉，授黃安丞。

translations.literal: Early in the Qianfeng era he responded to the Fengshan examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Huang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianfeng era he responded to the Fengshan examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Huang'an.

sentences.zh: 會刺史有女病篤，崇儼致他方殊物以療之，其疾乃愈。

translations.literal: It happened that the prefect's daughter was gravely ill; Chongyan procured rare things from distant places to treat her, and her illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the prefect's daughter was gravely ill; Chongyan procured rare things from distant places to treat her, and her illness was cured.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞其名，召與語。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong heard his name and summoned him to converse.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong heard his name and summoned him to converse.

sentences.zh: 悅之，擢授冀王府文學。

translations.literal: Pleased with him, he promoted him to Literary Scholar of the Princely Establishment of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased with him, the emperor promoted him to Literary Scholar of the Princely Establishment of Ji.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，累遷正諫大夫，特令入閣供奉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng he was promoted in succession to Regular Remonstrance Grand Master and was specially ordered to enter the privy council in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yifeng he was promoted in succession to Regular Remonstrance Grand Master and was specially ordered to enter the privy council in attendance.

sentences.zh: 崇儼每因謁見，輒假以神道，頗陳時政得失，帝深加允納。

translations.literal: Whenever Chongyan had an audience he would invoke supernatural ways and speak quite frankly on the gains and losses of current policy; the emperor deeply approved and accepted his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chongyan had an audience he would invoke supernatural ways and speak quite frankly on the gains and losses of current policy; the emperor deeply approved and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 潤州棲霞寺，是其五代祖梁處士山賓故宅，帝特為制碑文，親書于石，論者榮之。

translations.literal: Qixia Temple in Runzhou was the former residence of his fifth-generation ancestor, the Liang recluse Shan Bin; the emperor specially composed an inscription and personally wrote it on stone—commentators regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Qixia Temple in Runzhou was the former residence of his fifth-generation ancestor, the Liang recluse Shan Bin; the emperor specially composed an inscription and personally wrote it on stone, and commentators regarded this as an honor.

sentences.zh: 四年，為盜所殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was killed by robbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was killed by robbers.

sentences.zh: 時語以為崇儼密與天后為厭勝之法，又私奏章懷太子不堪承繼大位，太子密知之，潛使人害之。
