translations.literal: Rumor at the time held that Chongyan secretly practiced counter-curse rites with the Empress Tianhou and had privately memorialized that Crown Prince Zhanghuai was unfit to succeed the throne; the crown prince learned of this secretly and secretly sent men to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor at the time held that Chongyan secretly practiced counter-curse rites with Empress Tianhou and had privately memorialized that Crown Prince Zhanghuai was unfit to succeed the throne; the crown prince learned of this in secret and secretly sent men to harm him.

sentences.zh: 優制贈侍中，諡曰莊，仍拜其子珪為秘書郎。

translations.literal: By gracious edict he was posthumously granted Grand Counselor, given the posthumous name Zhuang, and his son Gui was appointed Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: By gracious edict he was posthumously granted Grand Counselor, given the posthumous name Zhuang, and his son Gui was appointed Secretary.

sentences.zh: 珪，開元中仕至懷州刺史。

translations.literal: Gui rose during the Kaiyuan era to prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gui rose during the Kaiyuan era to prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 張憬藏

translations.literal: Zhang Jingzang
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingzang

sentences.zh: 張憬藏，許州長社人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingzang was a native of Changshe in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingzang was a native of Changshe in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 少工相術，與袁天綱齊名。

translations.literal: In youth he was adept at physiognomy and shared fame with Yuan Tiangang.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was adept at physiognomy and shared fame with Yuan Tiangang.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事蔣儼年少時，嘗遇憬藏，因問祿命。

translations.literal: When Jiang Yan, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was young he once met Jingzang and asked about his fate and emolument.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Yan, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was young he once met Jingzang and asked about his fate and emolument.

sentences.zh: 憬藏曰：「公從今二年，當得東宮掌兵之官，秩未終而免職。

translations.literal: Jingzang said: "From now, in two years you will obtain an office in the Eastern Palace in charge of troops; before your term ends you will be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzang said, "From now, in two years you will obtain an office in the Eastern Palace in charge of troops; before your term ends you will be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 免職之後，厄在三尺土下。

translations.literal: After dismissal, your affliction will be beneath three feet of earth.
translations.idiomatic: After dismissal, your affliction will be beneath three feet of earth.

sentences.zh: 又經六年，據此合是死征。

translations.literal: After another six years, by this reckoning it should be a sign of death.
translations.idiomatic: After another six years, by this reckoning it should be a sign of death.

sentences.zh: 然後當享富貴，名位俱盛，即又不合中，年至六十一，為蒲州刺史，十月三十日午時祿絕。」

translations.literal: Yet afterward you should enjoy wealth and honor, with fame and rank both flourishing—though this too will not match precisely; at age sixty-one, as prefect of Puzhou, on the thirtieth day of the tenth month at the noon hour your emolument will run out."
translations.idiomatic: Yet afterward you should enjoy wealth and honor, with fame and rank both flourishing—though this too will not match precisely; at age sixty-one, as prefect of Puzhou, on the thirtieth day of the tenth month at the noon hour your allotted span will end."

sentences.zh: 儼後皆如其言。

translations.literal: Later Yan found all came to pass as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan found all came to pass as he had said.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉使高麗，被莫離支囚於地窖中，經六年，然後得歸。

translations.literal: He once served on mission to Goguryeo and was imprisoned by Molizhi in an underground cellar; after six years he was finally able to return.
translations.idiomatic: He once served on mission to Goguryeo and was imprisoned by Molizhi in an underground cellar; after six years he was finally able to return.

sentences.zh: 及在蒲州，年六十一矣，至期，召人吏妻子與之告別，自雲當死。

translations.literal: When he was in Puzhou, he was sixty-one; when the appointed day came he summoned clerks, subordinates, and his wife and children to take leave, saying himself that he must die.
translations.idiomatic: When he was in Puzhou, he was sixty-one; when the appointed day came he summoned clerks, subordinates, and his wife and children to take leave, saying himself that he must die.

sentences.zh: 俄而有敕，許令致仕。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward an edict arrived permitting him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward an edict arrived permitting him to retire.

sentences.zh: 左僕射劉仁軌微時，嘗與鄉人靖思賢各齎絹贈憬藏以問官祿。

translations.literal: When Liu Ren'gui, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was still obscure, he once brought silk together with his fellow townsman Jing Sixian as a gift to Jingzang to inquire about official rank and emolument.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ren'gui, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was still obscure, he once brought silk together with his fellow townsman Jing Sixian as a gift to Jingzang to inquire about official rank and emolument.

sentences.zh: 憬藏謂仁軌曰：「公居五品要官，雖暫解黜，終當位極人臣。」

translations.literal: Jingzang said to Ren'gui: "You will hold a key fifth-rank office; though temporarily dismissed, in the end you will reach the utmost of ministerial rank."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzang said to Ren'gui, "You will hold a key fifth-rank office; though temporarily dismissed, in the end you will reach the utmost of ministerial rank."

sentences.zh: 仁軌後自給事中坐事，令白衣向海東效力。

translations.literal: Later Ren'gui, as supervising secretary, was punished for an offense and ordered to serve in commoner's dress in the eastern sea region.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ren'gui, as supervising secretary, was punished for an offense and ordered to serve in commoner's dress in the eastern sea region.

sentences.zh: 固辭思賢之贈，曰：「公當孤獨客死。」

translations.literal: He firmly declined Sixian's gift, saying: "You will die alone as a stranger."
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined Sixian's gift, saying, "You will die alone as a stranger."

sentences.zh: 及仁軌為僕射，思賢尚存，謂人曰：「張憬藏相劉僕射，則妙矣。

translations.literal: When Ren'gui became Vice Director, Sixian was still alive and said to people: "Zhang Jingzang's reading of Vice Director Liu was marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren'gui became Vice Director, Sixian was still alive and said to people, "Zhang Jingzang's reading of Vice Director Liu was marvelous.

sentences.zh: 吾今已有三子，田宅自如，豈其言亦有不中也？」

translations.literal: I now have three sons and my fields and house are as they should be—can his words also have missed the mark?"
translations.idiomatic: I now have three sons and my fields and house are as they should be—can his words also have missed the mark?"

sentences.zh: 俄而三子相繼而死，盡貨田宅，寄死於所親園內。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward his three sons died in succession; he sold all his fields and house and arranged to die in a kinsman's garden.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward his three sons died in succession; he sold all his fields and house and arranged to die in a kinsman's garden.

sentences.zh: 憬藏相人之妙，皆此類。

translations.literal: Jingzang's marvelous skill in reading men was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzang's marvelous skill in reading men was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 竟不仕，以壽終。

translations.literal: He never took office and died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: He never took office and died of old age.

sentences.zh: 李嗣真

translations.literal: Li Sizhen
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhen

sentences.zh: 李嗣真，滑州匡城人也。

translations.literal: Li Sizhen was a native of Kuangcheng in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhen was a native of Kuangcheng in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 父彥琮，趙州長史。

translations.literal: His father Yanchong was chief secretary of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanchong was chief secretary of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嗣真博學曉音律，兼善陰陽推算之術。

translations.literal: Sizhen was broadly learned and versed in music, and also skilled in yin-yang calculation and prognostication.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen was broadly learned and versed in music, and also skilled in yin-yang calculation and prognostication.

sentences.zh: 弱冠明經舉，補許州司功。

translations.literal: At his coming of age he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Records Officer of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his coming of age he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Records Officer of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時左侍極賀蘭敏之受詔于東台修撰，奏嗣真弘文館參預其事。

translations.literal: At that time Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Helan Minzhi received orders to compile at the East Terrace and memorialized that Sizhen join the Hongwen Academy in participating in the work.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Helan Minzhi received orders to compile at the East Terrace and memorialized that Sizhen join the Hongwen Academy in participating in the work.

sentences.zh: 嗣真與同時學士劉獻臣、徐昭俱稱少俊，館中號為「三少」。

translations.literal: Sizhen, together with contemporaries among the academicians Liu Xianchen and Xu Zhao, were all called young talents; within the academy they were styled the "Three Young Men."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen, together with contemporaries among the academicians Liu Xianchen and Xu Zhao, were all called young talents; within the academy they were styled the "Three Young Men."

sentences.zh: 敏之既恃寵驕盈，嗣真知其必敗，謂所親曰：「此非庇身之所也。」

translations.literal: Once Minzhi, relying on favor, grew arrogant and overbearing, Sizhen knew he would surely fall and said to those close to him: "This is not a place to shelter oneself."
translations.idiomatic: Once Minzhi, relying on favor, grew arrogant and overbearing, Sizhen knew he would surely fall and said to those close to him, "This is not a place to shelter oneself."

sentences.zh: 因咸亨年京中大饑，乃求出，補義烏令。

translations.literal: Because in the Xianheng era the capital suffered great famine, he sought to leave and was appointed magistrate of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Because in the Xianheng era the capital suffered great famine, he sought to leave and was appointed magistrate of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 無何，敏之敗，修撰官皆連坐流放，嗣真獨不預焉。

translations.literal: Before long Minzhi fell; all compiling officials were implicated and exiled, but Sizhen alone was not involved.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Minzhi fell; all compiling officials were implicated and exiled, but Sizhen alone was not involved.

sentences.zh: 調露中，為始平令，風化大行。

translations.literal: During Tiaolu he served as magistrate of Shiping, where moral transformation was greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiaolu era he served as magistrate of Shiping, where moral transformation was greatly carried out.

sentences.zh: 時章懷太子居春宮，嗣真嘗於太清觀奏樂，謂道士劉概、輔儼曰：「此曲何哀思不和之甚也？」

translations.literal: At that time Crown Prince Zhanghuai resided in the Eastern Palace; Sizhen once performed music at Taqing Abbey and said to the Daoist priests Liu Kai and Fu Yan: "Why is this melody so grievously sad and disharmonious?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Crown Prince Zhanghuai resided in the Eastern Palace; Sizhen once performed music at Taqing Abbey and said to the Daoist priests Liu Kai and Fu Yan, "Why is this melody so grievously sad and disharmonious?"

sentences.zh: 概、儼曰：「此太子所作《寶慶樂》也。」

translations.literal: Kai and Yan said: "This is the Baojing Music composed by the crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: Kai and Yan said: "This is the Baojing Music composed by the crown prince."

sentences.zh: 居數日，太子廢為庶人。

translations.literal: Within several days the crown prince was deposed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Within several days the crown prince was deposed as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 概等以其事聞奏，高宗大奇之，征拜司禮丞，仍掌五禮儀注，加中散大夫，封常山子。

translations.literal: Kai and others reported this matter to the throne; Emperor Gaozong was greatly astonished, summoned him, and appointed him Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, still in charge of the ceremonial regulations of the five rites; he was also granted Grand Master of Palace Attendance and enfeoffed as Viscount of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai and others reported this matter to the throne; Emperor Gaozong was greatly astonished, summoned him, and appointed him Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, still in charge of the ceremonial regulations of the five rites; he was also granted Grand Master of Palace Attendance and enfeoffed as Viscount of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 永昌中，拜右御史中丞，知大夫事。

translations.literal: During the Yongchang era he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and managed the duties of the censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchang era he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and managed the duties of the censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時酷吏來俊臣構陷無罪，嗣真上書諫曰：「臣聞陳平事漢祖，謀疏楚君臣，乃用黃金五萬斤，行反間之術。

translations.literal: At that time the cruel official Lai Junchen framed the innocent; Sizhen submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your servant has heard that when Chen Ping served Emperor Gaozu of Han, he plotted to drive apart the lord and ministers of Chu and used fifty thousand jin of gold to carry out counter-intelligence tactics.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the cruel official Lai Junchen framed the innocent; Sizhen submitted a memorial remonstrating, "Your servant has heard that when Chen Ping served Emperor Gaozu of Han, he plotted to drive apart the lord and ministers of Chu and used fifty thousand jin of gold to carry out counter-intelligence tactics.

sentences.zh: 項王果疑臣下，陳平反間果行。

translations.literal: Lord Xiang indeed grew suspicious of his subordinates, and Chen Ping's counter-intelligence did succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xiang indeed grew suspicious of his subordinates, and Chen Ping's counter-intelligence did succeed.

sentences.zh: 今告事紛紜，虛多實少，焉知必無陳平先謀疏陛下君臣，後謀除國家良善，臣恐為社稷之禍！

translations.literal: Now denunciations swarm—empty more than real—who is to say there is certainly no Chen Ping who first plots to drive apart Your Majesty and his ministers, then plots to remove the state's good and worthy? Your servant fears disaster for the altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: Now denunciations swarm—empty more than real—who is to say there is certainly no Chen Ping who first plots to drive apart Your Majesty and his ministers, then plots to remove the state's good and worthy? Your servant fears disaster for the altars of soil and grain!

sentences.zh: 伏乞陛下特回天慮，察臣狂瞽，然後退就鼎鑊，實無所恨！」

translations.literal: I humbly beg Your Majesty especially to turn back the heavenly deliberation, examine your servant's rash blindness, and then let me withdraw to the cauldron—I shall truly have no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty especially to turn back the heavenly deliberation, examine your servant's rash blindness, and then let me withdraw to the cauldron—I shall truly have no regret!"

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋被俊臣所陷，配流嶺南。

translations.literal: Soon he was framed by Junchen and sentenced to exile in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was framed by Junchen and sentenced to exile in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天年，征還，至桂陽，自筮死日，預讬桂陽官屬備兇器。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era he was recalled; reaching Guiyang he divined his own day of death and beforehand entrusted the Guiyang officials to prepare funeral implements.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian era he was recalled; reaching Guiyang he divined his own day of death and beforehand entrusted the Guiyang officials to prepare funeral implements.

sentences.zh: 依期暴卒。

translations.literal: On the appointed day he suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day he suddenly died.

sentences.zh: 則天深加憫惜，敕州縣遞靈輿還鄉，贈濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian deeply mourned and cherished his memory, ordered the prefectures and counties to relay his funeral carriage homeward, and posthumously granted him prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian deeply mourned and cherished his memory, ordered the prefectures and counties to relay his funeral carriage homeward, and posthumously granted him prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，又贈御史大夫。

translations.literal: Early in the Shenlong era he was again posthumously granted Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he was again posthumously granted Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 撰《明堂新禮》十卷，《孝經指要》、《詩品》、《書品》、《畫品》各一卷。

translations.literal: He compiled New Rites of the Bright Hall in ten scrolls, and Essentials of the Classic of Filial Piety, Judgments on Poetry, Judgments on Calligraphy, and Judgments on Painting, each in one scroll.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled New Rites of the Bright Hall in ten scrolls, and Essentials of the Classic of Filial Piety, Judgments on Poetry, Judgments on Calligraphy, and Judgments on Painting, each in one scroll.

sentences.zh: 張文仲

translations.literal: Zhang Wenzong
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenzong

sentences.zh: 張文仲，洛州洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenzong was a native of Luoyang in Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenzong was a native of Luoyang in Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 少與鄉人李虔縱、京兆人韋慈藏並以醫術知名。

translations.literal: In youth he, together with his fellow townsman Li Qianzong and Wei Cizang of Jingzhao, were all famed for medical skill.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he, together with his fellow townsman Li Qianzong and Wei Cizang of Jingzhao, were all famed for medical skill.

sentences.zh: 文仲，則天初為侍御醫。

translations.literal: Wenzong, at the beginning of Zetian's reign, served as Attending Physician.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong, at the beginning of Zetian's reign, served as Attending Physician.

sentences.zh: 時特進蘇良嗣於殿庭因拜跪便絕倒，則天令文仲、慈藏隨至宅候之。

translations.literal: At that time Excellency Su Liangsi collapsed unconscious while bowing and kneeling in the palace hall; Zetian ordered Wenzong and Cizang to follow him to his residence and attend him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Excellency Su Liangsi collapsed unconscious while bowing and kneeling in the palace hall; Zetian ordered Wenzong and Cizang to follow him to his residence and attend him.

sentences.zh: 文仲曰：「此因憂憤邪氣激也。

translations.literal: Wenzong said: "This is because gloomy resentment and evil qi were stirred up.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong said, "This is because gloomy resentment and evil qi were stirred up.

sentences.zh: 若痛沖脅，則劇難救。」

translations.literal: If the pain reaches the chest and flank, then it will be extremely hard to save."
translations.idiomatic: If the pain reaches the chest and flank, then it will be extremely hard to save."

sentences.zh: 自朝候之。

translations.literal: They attended him from the morning court session onward.
translations.idiomatic: They attended him from the morning court session onward.

sentences.zh: 未及食時，即苦沖脅絞痛。

translations.literal: Before mealtime he was already wracked with wrenching pain in the chest and flank.
translations.idiomatic: Before mealtime he was already wracked with wrenching pain in the chest and flank.

sentences.zh: 文仲曰：「若入心，即不可療。」

translations.literal: Wenzong said: "If it enters the heart, then it cannot be treated."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong said, "If it enters the heart, then it cannot be treated."

sentences.zh: 俄頃心痛，不復下藥，日旰而卒。

translations.literal: In a moment he suffered heart pain; medicine was no longer given, and at sundown he died.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment he suffered heart pain; medicine was no longer given, and at sundown he died.

sentences.zh: 文仲尤善療風疾。

translations.literal: Wenzong was especially skilled at treating wind disorders.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong was especially skilled at treating wind disorders.

sentences.zh: 其後則天令文仲集當時名醫共撰療風氣諸方，仍令麟台監王方慶監其修撰。

translations.literal: Afterwards Zetian ordered Wenzong to gather the renowned physicians of the time to compile together formulas for treating wind and qi disorders, and also appointed Wang Fangqing, Director of the Palace Library, to supervise the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Afterwards Zetian ordered Wenzong to gather the renowned physicians of the time to compile formulas for treating wind and qi disorders, and also appointed Wang Fangqing, Director of the Palace Library, to supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 文仲奏曰：「風有一百二十四種，氣有八十種。

translations.literal: Wenzong memorialized: "Wind has one hundred twenty-four types; qi has eighty types.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong memorialized, "Wind has one hundred twenty-four types; qi has eighty types.

sentences.zh: 大抵醫藥雖同，人性各異，庸醫不達藥之性使冬夏失節，因此殺人。

translations.literal: Generally, though medicines may be the same, human natures differ; mediocre physicians who do not grasp the properties of drugs make winter and summer lose their proper seasons, and thus kill people.
translations.idiomatic: In general, though the same medicine may be prescribed, patients differ; mediocre physicians who do not understand how drugs behave in season, winter or summer, end up killing people.

sentences.zh: 唯腳氣頭風上氣，常須服藥不絕。

translations.literal: Only for foot qi, head wind, and upper qi must one take medicine without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Only for foot qi, head wind, and upper qi must one take medicine without interruption.

sentences.zh: 自餘則隨其發動，臨時消息之。

translations.literal: For the rest, one treats according to when they flare up, adjusting provisionally as the occasion requires.
translations.idiomatic: For all other conditions, one treats them as they arise, adjusting the remedy to fit each episode.

sentences.zh: 但有風氣之人，春末夏初及秋暮，要得通泄，即不困劇。」

translations.literal: Those who suffer from wind and qi disorders, at the end of spring and beginning of summer and in late autumn, must obtain free discharge; then they will not be severely afflicted."
translations.idiomatic: Those prone to wind and qi disorders must purge freely at the end of spring, the start of summer, and in late autumn; then they will not suffer severely."

sentences.zh: 於是撰四時常服及輕重大小諸方十八首表上之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he compiled eighteen formulas for seasonal regular use and for conditions of varying severity, great and small, and submitted them in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He then compiled eighteen formulas—for seasonal regular use and for conditions mild or severe, great or small—and submitted them in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 文仲久視年終於尚藥奉禦。

translations.literal: In the Jiushi era Wenzong died while serving as Director of Pharmacy Attending the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiushi era Wenzong died while serving as Director of Pharmacy Attending the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 撰《隨身備急方》三卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He compiled Portable Emergency Formulas in three scrolls, which circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Portable Emergency Formulas in three scrolls, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 李虔縱 韋慈藏 附

translations.literal: Li Qianzong, Wei Cizang, appended
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianzong and Wei Cizang, appended biographies

sentences.zh: 虔縱，官至侍御醫。

translations.literal: Qianzong rose to the post of Attending Physician.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzong rose to Attending Physician.

sentences.zh: 慈藏，景龍中光祿卿。

translations.literal: Cizang, during the Jinglong era, served as Minister of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Cizang served as Minister of Imperial Entertainments during the Jinglong era.

sentences.zh: 自則天、中宗已後，諸醫咸推文仲等三人為首。

translations.literal: From the reigns of Zetian and Zhongzong onward, physicians everywhere acclaimed Wenzong and these three men as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: From the reigns of Zetian and Zhongzong onward, physicians everywhere ranked Wenzong and these three men first among their peers.

sentences.zh: 尚獻甫

translations.literal: Shang Xianfu
translations.idiomatic: Shang Xianfu

sentences.zh: 尚獻甫，衛州汲人也。

translations.literal: Shang Xianfu was a native of Ji in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Xianfu was a native of Ji in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 尤善天文。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in astronomy.

sentences.zh: 初，出家為道士。

translations.literal: At first he left home and became a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: At first he left home and became a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 則天時召見，起家拜太史令，固辭曰：「臣久從放誕，不能屈事官長。」

translations.literal: During Zetian's reign he was summoned to audience; on first appointment he was made Director of the Grand Astrologer, but firmly declined, saying: "Your subject has long followed a life of unfettered freedom and cannot bow to serving superiors."
translations.idiomatic: During Zetian's reign he was summoned to court and, on entering official service, was appointed Director of the Grand Astrologer; he firmly declined, saying, "Your subject has long lived in unfettered freedom and cannot submit to serving superiors."

sentences.zh: 則天乃改太史局為渾儀監，不隸秘書省，以獻甫為渾儀監。

translations.literal: Zetian thereupon converted the Bureau of the Grand Astrologer into the Directorate of the Armillary Sphere, not subordinate to the Secretariat, and appointed Xianfu Director of the Armillary Sphere.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian thereupon converted the Bureau of the Grand Astrologer into the Directorate of the Armillary Sphere, independent of the Secretariat, and appointed Xianfu its director.

sentences.zh: 數顧問災異，事皆符驗。

translations.literal: She repeatedly consulted him on portents and calamities, and events always matched his predictions.
translations.idiomatic: She repeatedly consulted him on portents and calamities, and events always bore out his predictions.

sentences.zh: 又令獻甫于上陽宮集學者撰《方域圖》。

translations.literal: She also had Xianfu gather scholars at Shangyang Palace to compile the Map of the Territories.
translations.idiomatic: She also had Xianfu gather scholars at Shangyang Palace to compile the Map of the Territories.

sentences.zh: 長安二年，獻甫奏曰：「臣本命納音在金，今熒惑犯五諸候、太史之位。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, Xianfu memorialized: "Your subject's natal pitchpipe tone belongs to Metal; now Mars violates the Five Marquis and the position of the Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chang'an, Xianfu memorialized, "Your subject's natal pitchpipe tone belongs to Metal; Mars now violates the Five Marquis and the Grand Astrologer's station.

sentences.zh: 熒，火也，能克金，是臣將死之征。」

translations.literal: Mars is Fire and can overcome Metal—this is a sign that your subject is about to die."
translations.idiomatic: Mars is Fire and can overcome Metal—this is a sign that I am about to die."

sentences.zh: 則天曰：「朕為卿禳之。」

translations.literal: Zetian said: "I shall perform exorcistic rites for you."
translations.idiomatic: Zetian said: "I shall perform exorcistic rites on your behalf."

sentences.zh: 遽轉獻甫為水衡都尉，謂曰：「水能生金，今又去太史之位，卿無憂矣。」

translations.literal: She immediately transferred Xianfu to Colonel of the Water Balance and said: "Water can generate Metal, and now you are also away from the Astrologer's position—you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: She immediately transferred Xianfu to Colonel of the Water Balance and said: "Water generates Metal, and you are now removed from the Astrologer's station as well—you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 其秋，獻甫卒，則天甚嗟異惜之。

translations.literal: That autumn Xianfu died, and Zetian deeply sighed in wonder and regret.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Xianfu died, and Zetian sighed in wonder and deep regret.

sentences.zh: 復以渾儀監為太史局，依舊隸秘書監。

translations.literal: The Directorate of the Armillary Sphere was again made the Bureau of the Grand Astrologer, subordinate as before to the Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of the Armillary Sphere was restored as the Bureau of the Grand Astrologer, again subordinate to the Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 裴知古 附

translations.literal: Pei Zhigu, appended
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhigu, appended biography

sentences.zh: 時又有雍州人裴知古，善於音律。

translations.literal: At that time there was also Pei Zhigu of Yongzhou, skilled in musical pitch and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was also Pei Zhigu of Yongzhou, skilled in musical pitch and regulation.

sentences.zh: 長安中為太樂丞。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Music Office.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年正月，春享西京太廟，知古預其事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Shenlong, at the spring offering in the Western Capital's Imperial Ancestral Temple, Zhigu took part in the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Shenlong, at the spring offering in the Western Capital's Imperial Ancestral Temple, Zhigu took part in the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 謂萬年令元行沖曰：「金石諧和，當有吉慶之事，其在唐室子孫乎？」

translations.literal: He said to Yuan Xingchong, magistrate of Wannian: "Metal and stone are in harmony—there should be an auspicious celebration; might it concern descendants of the Tang house?"
translations.idiomatic: He said to Yuan Xingchong, magistrate of Wannian, "Metal and stone are in harmony—there should be an auspicious celebration. Might it concern descendants of the Tang house?"

sentences.zh: 其月，中宗即位，復改國為唐。

translations.literal: That month Zhongzong ascended the throne and again changed the dynastic name to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Zhongzong ascended the throne and restored the dynastic name to Tang.

sentences.zh: 知古又能聽婚夕環佩之聲，知其夫妻終始。

translations.literal: Zhigu could also listen to the jade pendants at a wedding evening and know how the husband and wife's union would begin and end.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu could also listen to the sound of jade pendants on a wedding night and foretell how a marriage would begin and end.

sentences.zh: 後卒于太樂令。

translations.literal: Later he died while serving as Director of the Imperial Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Director of the Imperial Music Office.

sentences.zh: 孟詵，汝州梁人也。

translations.literal: Meng Shen was a native of Liang in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Shen was a native of Liang in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，累遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chuigong he was promoted through several posts to Drafting Secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chuigong he rose through several posts to Drafting Secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 詵少好方術，嘗于鳳閣侍郎劉禕之家，見其敕賜金，謂禕之曰：「此藥金也。

translations.literal: Shen from youth loved arts of formulas and techniques; once at the home of Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Liu Yizhi he saw gold bestowed by imperial decree and said to Yizhi: "This is alchemical gold.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shen loved the arts of formulas and techniques; once at the home of Vice Minister Liu Yizhi of the Phoenix Pavilion he saw gold bestowed by imperial decree and said to Yizhi, "This is alchemical gold.

sentences.zh: 若燒火其上，當有五色氣。」

translations.literal: If fire is applied to it, there should be five-colored vapor."
translations.idiomatic: If you apply fire to it, five-colored vapor should rise."

sentences.zh: 試之果然。

translations.literal: When tested, it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: When they tested it, it was exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 則天聞而不悅，因事出為台州司馬。

translations.literal: Zetian heard of this and was displeased; on a pretext he was sent out as Military Assistant of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian heard of this and was displeased; on a pretext he was sent out to serve as Military Assistant of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 後累遷春官侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted through several posts to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted through several posts to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 睿宗在籓，召充侍讀。

translations.literal: When Ruizong was prince, he was summoned to serve as Lecturer-in-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong held a princely fief, he was summoned to serve as Lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 長安中，為同州刺史，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he served as Prefect of Tongzhou and was granted Silver Azure Seal Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he served as Prefect of Tongzhou and was granted the title Silver Azure Seal Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 神龍初致仕，歸伊陽之山第，以藥餌為事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he retired and returned to his mountain estate at Yiyang, devoting himself to medicinal compounds.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenlong he retired to his mountain estate at Yiyang and devoted himself to medicinal compounds.

sentences.zh: 詵年雖晚暮，志力如壯，嘗謂所親曰：「若能保身養性者，常須善言莫離口，良藥莫離手。」

translations.literal: Though Shen's years were late, his will and strength were as in prime; he once told those close to him: "If one would preserve body and nurture nature, one must constantly keep kind words never far from the mouth and good medicine never far from the hand."
translations.idiomatic: Though Shen was advanced in years, his will and strength remained vigorous; he once told those close to him, "If you would preserve your body and nurture your nature, keep kind words ever on your lips and good medicine ever in your hand."

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，召赴京師，將加任用，固辭衰老。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, he was summoned to the capital and about to be given further appointment, but firmly declined on account of old age.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne, he was summoned to the capital for further appointment but firmly declined on account of old age.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，優詔賜物一百段，又令每歲春秋二時，特給羊酒糜粥。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun an exceptional edict granted him one hundred rolls of goods, and ordered that each year in the two seasons of spring and autumn special provisions of mutton, wine, and porridge be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun an exceptional edict granted him one hundred rolls of goods and ordered that each spring and autumn he receive special provisions of mutton, wine, and porridge.

sentences.zh: 開元初，河南尹畢構以詵有古人之風，改其所居為子平裏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan Bi Gou, Intendant of Henan, because Shen had the air of ancient worthies, renamed his neighborhood Ziping Lane.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan Bi Gou, Intendant of Henan, finding that Shen had the bearing of the ancients, renamed his neighborhood Ziping Lane.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年九十三。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, aged ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at the age of ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 詵所居官，好勾剝為政，雖繁而理。

translations.literal: In the offices Shen held, he liked meticulous investigation in governance; though burdened with detail, affairs were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In the offices he held, Shen favored meticulous investigation in governance; though his methods were demanding, affairs were well ordered.

sentences.zh: 撰《家》、《祭禮》各一卷，《喪服要》二卷，《補養方》、《必效方》各三卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Family Rites and Sacrificial Rites, each one scroll; Essentials of Mourning Garb, two scrolls; and Nourishing Formulas and Sure-Effect Formulas, each three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Family Rites and Sacrificial Rites, each in one scroll; Essentials of Mourning Garb in two scrolls; and Nourishing Formulas and Sure-Effect Formulas, each in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 嚴善思

translations.literal: Yan Shansi
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shansi

sentences.zh: 嚴善思，同州朝邑人也。

translations.literal: Yan Shansi was a native of Chaoyi in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shansi was a native of Chaoyi in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 少以學涉知名，尤善天文歷數及卜相之術。

translations.literal: From youth he was known for broad learning, and was especially skilled in astronomy, calendrics, and the arts of divination and physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for broad learning and was especially skilled in astronomy, calendrics, and the arts of divination and physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 初應消聲幽藪科舉擢第。

translations.literal: At first he passed the special examination for Hidden Talents in Secluded Groves.
translations.idiomatic: He first passed the special examination for Hidden Talents in Secluded Groves.

sentences.zh: 則天時為監察御史，權右拾遺、內供奉。

translations.literal: During Zetian's reign he served as Investigating Censor, with additional duties as Right Reminder and Internal Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Zetian's reign he served as Investigating Censor, with additional duties as Right Reminder and Internal Attendant.

sentences.zh: 數上表陳時政得失，多見納用。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials setting forth the merits and faults of current policy, and many were accepted and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials on the merits and faults of current policy, and many of his recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 稍遷太史令。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Director of the Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Director of the Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 聖曆二年，熒惑入輿鬼，則天以問善思。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengli, Mars entered the Chariot and Ghost asterism; Zetian asked Shansi about it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengli, Mars entered the Chariot and Ghost asterism, and Zetian asked Shansi what it portended.

sentences.zh: 善思對曰：「商姓大臣當之。」

translations.literal: Shansi replied: "A minister of the Metal surname will meet this."
translations.idiomatic: Shansi replied, "A great minister of Metal surname will bear this omen."

sentences.zh: 其年，文昌左相王及善卒。

translations.literal: That year Left Chancellor of the Secretariat Wang Jishan died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Jishan, Left Chancellor of the Secretariat, died.

sentences.zh: 長安中，熒惑入月，鎮星犯天關。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, Mars entered the Moon, and Saturn violated Tian'guan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era, Mars entered the Moon and Saturn violated Tian'guan.

sentences.zh: 善思奏曰：「法有亂臣伏罪，且有臣下謀上之象。」

translations.literal: Shansi memorialized: "By the laws [of portents] there is an image of a rebellious minister punished, and also of subordinates plotting against their ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Shansi memorialized, "The portents show a rebellious minister brought to justice and also subordinates plotting against their ruler."

sentences.zh: 歲餘，張柬之、敬暉等起兵誅張易之、昌宗。

translations.literal: More than a year later, Zhang Jianzhi, Jing Hui, and others raised troops and executed Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Zhang Jianzhi, Jing Hui, and others raised troops and executed Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong.

sentences.zh: 其占驗皆此類也。

translations.literal: His prognostications verified were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His verified prognostications were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，遷給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenlong he was promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 則天崩，將合葬乾陵，善思奏議曰：

translations.literal: When Zetian died and they were about to bury her jointly in Qianling, Shansi submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: When Zetian died and they were about to bury her jointly in Qianling, Shansi submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 謹按《天元房錄葬法》云：「尊者先葬，卑者不合於後開入。」

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the Tianyuan Fanglu Burial Methods: "The superior is buried first; the inferior should not afterward be opened and placed inside."
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully according to the Tianyuan Fanglu Burial Methods, "The superior is buried first; the inferior should not afterward be opened and placed inside."

sentences.zh: 則天太后，卑于天皇大帝，今欲開乾陵合葬，即是以卑動尊。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian was inferior to Emperor Tianhuang; now to open Qianling for joint burial is to move the inferior against the superior.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian stood below Emperor Tianhuang; to open Qianling now for joint burial would be to let the inferior disturb the superior.

sentences.zh: 事既不經，恐非安隱。

translations.literal: The matter is without precedent and may not be safe and secure.
translations.idiomatic: The matter lacks precedent and may not be safe.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞乾陵玄闕，其門以石閉塞，其石縫隙，鑄鐵以固其中。

translations.literal: Your subject also hears that at the dark gate of Qianling the doors are blocked with stone, and in the seams of the stone iron is cast to fix them within.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject also hears that at the dark gate of Qianling the doors are sealed with stone, and iron is cast into the seams to hold them fast.

sentences.zh: 今若開陵，必須鐫鑿。

translations.literal: If the tomb is opened now, it must be carved and chiseled.
translations.idiomatic: If the tomb is opened now, it must be carved and chiseled open.

sentences.zh: 然以神明之道，體尚幽玄；

translations.literal: Yet the way of the spirits reveres what is hidden and numinous;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the way of the spirits reveres what is hidden and numinous;

sentences.zh: 今乃動眾加功，誠恐多所驚黷。

translations.literal: to now mobilize the multitude and add labor truly fears much desecration of the sacred.
translations.idiomatic: to mobilize a crowd and add labor now would, I fear, provoke much desecration of the sacred.

sentences.zh: 又若別開門道，以入玄宮，即往者葬時，神位先定，今更改作，為害益深。

translations.literal: Moreover, if a separate gate path is opened to enter the inner palace, then at the former burial the spirit seat was already fixed; to alter it now would deepen the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if a separate gate path is opened to enter the inner palace, the spirit seat was fixed at the original burial; to alter it now would deepen the harm.

sentences.zh: 又以修築乾陵之後，國頻有難，遂至則天太后權總萬機，二十餘年，其難始定。

translations.literal: Moreover, after Qianling was built the state repeatedly suffered calamities, until Empress Zetian took control of all affairs for more than twenty years before the troubles finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after Qianling was built the state suffered repeated calamities, until Empress Zetian seized control of all affairs for more than twenty years before order was restored.

sentences.zh: 今乃更加營作，伏恐還有難生。

translations.literal: To add construction now—I fear calamities may arise again.
translations.idiomatic: To add construction now—I fear calamities may arise again.

sentences.zh: 但合葬非古，著在禮經，緣情為用，無足依准。

translations.literal: Joint burial is not ancient custom; it is recorded in ritual classics as following human feeling—no reliable standard to cite.
translations.idiomatic: Joint burial is not ancient custom; the ritual classics record it only as an accommodation to human feeling—not a reliable standard to follow.

sentences.zh: 況今事有不安，豈可復循斯制！

translations.literal: Moreover, when the present matter is unsafe, how can we again follow that institution!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the present matter is unsafe, how can we follow that institution again!

sentences.zh: 伏見漢時諸陵，皇后多不合葬；

translations.literal: Your subject observes that in Han times at the various tombs, empresses mostly were not jointly buried;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject observes that in Han times, at the various imperial tombs, empresses were mostly not jointly buried;

sentences.zh: 魏、晉已降，始有合者。

translations.literal: from Wei and Jin downward, joint burial began.
translations.idiomatic: from Wei and Jin downward, joint burial began to appear.

sentences.zh: 然以兩漢積年，向餘四百；

translations.literal: Yet the two Han dynasties accumulated years totaling nearly four hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two Han dynasties endured for nearly four hundred years combined;

sentences.zh: 魏、晉之後，祚皆不長。

translations.literal: after Wei and Jin, their reigns were none long.
translations.idiomatic: after Wei and Jin, none of those dynasties endured long.

sentences.zh: 雖受命應期，有因天假，然以循機享德，亦在天時。

translations.literal: Though receiving the Mandate and answering the age had cause in Heaven's lending, yet to follow opportunity and enjoy virtue also depends on Heaven's season.
translations.idiomatic: Though receiving the Mandate and answering the age may owe something to Heaven's favor, to seize opportunity and enjoy virtue also depends on Heaven's season.

sentences.zh: 但陵墓所安，必資勝地，後之胤嗣，用托靈根，或有不安，後嗣亦難長享。

translations.literal: Yet where the imperial tomb rests must rely on an excellent site; later heirs trust their spiritual root to it—if there is unrest, successors also will find it hard to enjoy long prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet where an imperial tomb rests must rely on an excellent site; later heirs entrust their spiritual root to it—if the site is disturbed, successors will find it hard to enjoy long prosperity.

sentences.zh: 伏望依漢朝之故事，改魏、晉之頹綱，於乾陵之傍，更擇吉地，取生墓之法，別起一陵，既得從葬之儀，又成固本之業。

translations.literal: Your subject hopes to follow Han precedent, reform the decadent norms of Wei and Jin, choose anew an auspicious site beside Qianling, adopt the method of a living tomb, and build a separate mound—thus obtaining the ceremony of accompanying burial while also securing the foundation of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject hopes to follow Han precedent, reform the decadent norms of Wei and Jin, choose anew an auspicious site beside Qianling, adopt the method of a living tomb, and build a separate mound—thus honoring the rites of accompanying burial while securing the dynasty's foundation.

sentences.zh: 臣伏以合葬者，人緣私情；

translations.literal: Your subject submits that joint burial serves private human feeling;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject submits that joint burial serves private human feeling;

sentences.zh: 不合者，前修故事。

translations.literal: not joint burial follows the precedents of former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: not to bury jointly follows the precedents of former worthies.

sentences.zh: 若以神道有知，幽途自得通會；

translations.literal: If the spirit way has awareness, the dark path will naturally allow communion;
translations.idiomatic: If the spirit way has awareness, the dark path will naturally allow communion;

sentences.zh: 若以死者無知，合之復有何益！

translations.literal: if the dead have no awareness, what benefit is there in joining them!
translations.idiomatic: if the dead have no awareness, what benefit is there in burying them together!

sentences.zh: 然以山川精氣，土為星象，若葬得其所，則神安後昌；

translations.literal: Yet mountains and rivers have refined qi; earth forms star images—if burial finds its proper place, then spirits are at peace and descendants flourish;
translations.idiomatic: Yet mountains and rivers hold refined qi; earth forms star images—if burial finds its proper place, spirits are at peace and descendants flourish;

sentences.zh: 若葬失其宜，則神危後損。

translations.literal: if burial misses its fit, then spirits are endangered and descendants suffer loss.
translations.idiomatic: if burial misses its proper place, spirits are endangered and descendants suffer loss.

sentences.zh: 所以先哲垂范，具之葬經，欲使生人之道必安，死者之神必泰。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages of old left models, fully set forth in the burial classics, wishing to make the way of the living surely secure and the spirits of the dead surely at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sages of old left models, fully set forth in the burial classics, wishing to make the way of the living secure and the spirits of the dead at peace.

sentences.zh: 伏望少回天眷，俯覽臣言，行古昔之明規，割私情之愛欲，使社稷長享，天下乂安。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly hopes Heaven's favor may turn even slightly, that Your Majesty may look down upon your subject's words, follow the clear norms of antiquity, cut off private affection and desire, and make the altars of soil and grain long enjoyed and all under Heaven well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject humbly hopes Your Majesty will turn His heavenly favor even slightly, heed these words, follow the clear precedents of antiquity, set aside private affection and desire, and so secure the altars of state and bring peace to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 凡在懷生，孰不慶倖！

translations.literal: All who cherish life—who would not rejoice in good fortune!
translations.idiomatic: All who cherish life—who would not count themselves fortunate!

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，遷禮部侍郎，出為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and sent out as Prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and appointed Prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 睿宗在籓，善思嘗謂姚元之曰：「相王必登帝位。」

translations.literal: When Ruizong held a princely fief, Shansi once said to Yao Yuanshi: "The Prince of Xiang will surely ascend the imperial throne."
translations.idiomatic: While Ruizong was still a prince, Shansi once told Yao Yuanshi, "The Prince of Xiang will surely take the throne."

sentences.zh: 及踐祚，元之以事聞奏，由是召拜右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Yuanshi reported the matter, and Shansi was therefore summoned and appointed Right Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Yuanshi reported what Shansi had said, and Shansi was summoned and appointed Right Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 唐隆元年，鄭愔謀冊譙王重福為帝，乃草偽制，除善思為禮部尚書，知吏部選事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tanglong, Zheng Yin plotted to install Prince of Qiao Zhongfu as emperor; he drafted a spurious edict appointing Shansi Minister of Rites and put him in charge of personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tanglong, Zheng Yin plotted to install Prince of Qiao Zhongfu as emperor, drafted a forged edict appointing Shansi Minister of Rites, and put him in charge of personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及譙王下獄，景雲元年，大理寺奏：「善思與逆人重福通謀，合從極法。」

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qiao was imprisoned, in the first year of Jingyun the Court of Judicial Review memorialized: "Shansi conspired with the rebel Zhongfu; punishment should follow the utmost law."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qiao was imprisoned, in the first year of Jingyun the Court of Judicial Review memorialized: "Shansi conspired with the rebel Zhongfu and should be punished by the utmost penalty."

sentences.zh: 給事中韓思復奏曰：「議獄緩死，列聖明規；

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Han Sifu memorialized: "To debate cases and slow the execution of death is the enlightened norm of successive sages;
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Han Sifu memorialized: "Debating cases and deferring execution is the enlightened norm of successive sage emperors;

sentences.zh: 刑疑惟輕，有國恆典。

translations.literal: when punishment is doubtful, lean toward leniency—this is the constant standard of a state.
translations.idiomatic: when the law is in doubt, lean toward leniency—this is the enduring standard of any state.

sentences.zh: 嚴善思往在先朝，屬韋氏擅內，恃寵宮掖，謀危社稷。

translations.literal: Yan Shansi served in the previous reign; when Empress Wei monopolized the inner palace, relying on favor in the women's quarters and plotting to endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shansi had served in the previous reign when Empress Wei monopolized the inner palace, relying on favor in the women's quarters and plotting to endanger the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 善思此時，乃能先覺，因詣相府，有所發明，進論聖躬，必登宸極。

translations.literal: At that time Shansi was able to perceive it first; he therefore went to the Prince of Xiang's residence, made his views known, and argued that His Sacred Person would surely ascend the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shansi saw the danger first, went to the Prince of Xiang's residence, made his views known, and argued that His Sacred Person would surely ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 雖交遊重福，謀陷韋氏，敕追善思，書至便發，向懷逆節，寧即奔命？

translations.literal: Though he associated with Zhongfu and plotted against Empress Wei, when an edict summoned Shansi and the letter arrived he set out at once—if he had truly harbored treasonous intent, would he have obeyed so promptly?
translations.idiomatic: Though he had associated with Zhongfu and plotted against Empress Wei, when an edict summoned Shansi he set out the moment the letter arrived—if he had truly harbored treasonous intent, would he have obeyed so promptly?

sentences.zh: 一面疏綱，誠合順生；

translations.literal: To loosen the net on one side truly accords with letting life follow its course;
translations.idiomatic: To loosen the net on one side truly accords with sparing life;

sentences.zh: 三驅取禽，來而有宥。

translations.literal: in a three-sided hunt to take game, those that come forward receive pardon.
translations.idiomatic: in a three-sided hunt, those that come forward are spared.

sentences.zh: 唯刑是恤，理合昭詳。

translations.literal: Concern for punishment alone requires the matter be made clear and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: When punishment alone is at stake, the matter ought to be examined with full clarity.

sentences.zh: 請付刑部集群官議定奏裁，以符慎獄。」

translations.literal: Your subject asks that the case be referred to the Ministry of Justice to gather officials, deliberate, and memorialize for decision, in accord with careful adjudication."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks that the case be referred to the Ministry of Justice for deliberation among the officials and a memorial for imperial decision, in keeping with careful adjudication."

sentences.zh: 時議者多云：「善思合從原宥。」

translations.literal: At the time many in discussion said: "Shansi should receive clemency."
translations.idiomatic: At the time many argued: "Shansi should be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 有司仍執前議請誅之。

translations.literal: The responsible offices still held to the earlier view and requested execution.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices still held to the earlier view and requested his execution.

sentences.zh: 思復又駁奏懇直。

translations.literal: Sifu again submitted a forceful rebuttal, earnest and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu submitted another forceful rebuttal, earnest and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 睿宗納其奏，竟免善思死，配流靜州。

translations.literal: Ruizong accepted his memorial and ultimately spared Shansi's life, sentencing him to exile in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong accepted his memorial and ultimately spared Shansi's life, banishing him to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 無幾，遇赦還。

translations.literal: Before long he received amnesty and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was amnestied and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 年八十五，開元十七年卒。

translations.literal: He was eighty-five when he died in the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-five in the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，善思為御史時，中書舍人劉允濟為酷吏所陷，當死。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shansi was an investigating censor, Zhongshu Sheren Liu Yunji was framed by a harsh official and faced death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shansi was an investigating censor, Secretariat Drafter Liu Yunji was framed by a harsh official and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 善思湣其老，密表奏請，允濟乃得免誅。

translations.literal: Shansi pitied his age and secretly memorialized on his behalf; Yunji was thus spared execution.
translations.idiomatic: Shansi pitied his age and secretly memorialized on his behalf, and Yunji was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 善思後見允濟，竟不自言其事。

translations.literal: When Shansi later met Yunji, he never mentioned what he had done.
translations.idiomatic: When Shansi later met Yunji, he never once mentioned what he had done.

sentences.zh: 韓思復奏免善思之罪，亦未曾有所言謝。

translations.literal: When Han Sifu memorialized to spare Shansi's punishment, Shansi likewise never spoke a word of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Sifu memorialized to spare Shansi from punishment, Shansi likewise never spoke a word of thanks.

sentences.zh: 時人稱其長者。

translations.literal: People of the time praised him as a man of maturity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time praised him as a man of true maturity.

sentences.zh: 善思子向，乾元中為鳳翔尹，寶應中授太常員外卿。

translations.literal: Shansi's son Xiang served as Prefect of Fengxiang during Qianyuan and was appointed Assistant Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices during Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: Shansi's son Xiang served as Prefect of Fengxiang during the Qianyuan era and was appointed Assistant Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices during Baoying.

sentences.zh: 始善思父徐州長史延及善思，俱年八十五而卒；

translations.literal: From the beginning, Shansi's father Yan, Senior Administrator of Xuzhou, and Shansi himself both died at eighty-five;
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning, Shansi's father Yan, Senior Administrator of Xuzhou, and Shansi himself had both died at eighty-five;

sentences.zh: 廣德二年，向卒，又年八十五。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde, Xiang died—again at eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangde, Xiang died—again at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 向兄前趙郡司馬宙，長向十歲，向卒時，宙並無恙。

translations.literal: Xiang's elder brother Zhou, former Military Advisor of Zhao commandery, was ten years older than Xiang; when Xiang died, Zhou was still in good health.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's elder brother Zhou, former Military Advisor of Zhao commandery, was ten years his senior; when Xiang died, Zhou was still in good health.

sentences.zh: 金梁鳳

translations.literal: Jin Liangfeng
translations.idiomatic: Jin Liangfeng

sentences.zh: 金梁鳳，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Jin Liangfeng—no one knew where he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Liangfeng—no one knew where he came from.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，客於河西。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao he was a guest in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao he was staying in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 善相人，又言玄象。

translations.literal: He was skilled at reading faces and also spoke of celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at physiognomy and also spoke of celestial omens.

sentences.zh: 時哥舒翰為節度使，詔入京師。

translations.literal: At the time Geshu Han was military commissioner and was ordered to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Geshu Han was military commissioner and had been summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 裴冕為祠部郎中，知河西留後，在武威。

translations.literal: Pei Mian was Director in the Ministry of Rites, acting as deputy commissioner for Hexi, stationed at Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian was Director in the Ministry of Rites, serving as acting deputy commissioner for Hexi at Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 梁鳳謂冕曰：「玄象有變，半年間有兵起，郎中此時當得中丞，不拜中丞，即得宰相，不離天子左右，大富貴。」

translations.literal: Liangfeng said to Mian: "Celestial signs are changing; within half a year war will rise. At that time you, Sir, will become Vice Censor-in-Chief; if you do not take that post, you will become chancellor, never leaving the Son of Heaven's side—a great fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Liangfeng said to Mian, "The celestial signs are changing; within half a year war will break out. At that time you, Sir, will become Vice Censor-in-Chief; if you do not accept that post, you will become chancellor, never leaving the Son of Heaven's side—great wealth and honor await."

sentences.zh: 冕曰：「公乃狂言，冕何至此？」

translations.literal: Mian said: "Sir, that is mad talk—how could Mian reach such heights?"
translations.idiomatic: Mian said, "That is mad talk—how could I ever rise so high?"

sentences.zh: 梁鳳曰：「有一日向東京，一日入蜀川，一日來向朔方，此時公得相。」

translations.literal: Liangfeng said: "One day toward the Eastern Capital, one day into Shu, one day toward Shuofang—at that time, Sir, you will become chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Liangfeng said, "One day toward the Eastern Capital, one day into Shu, one day toward Shuofang—at that moment, Sir, you will become chancellor."

sentences.zh: 冕懼其言，深謝絕之。

translations.literal: Mian feared his words and firmly declined, cutting off further talk.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was alarmed by his words and firmly cut off further conversation.

sentences.zh: 其後安祿山反，南犯洛陽，僭稱偽位。

translations.literal: Afterward An Lushan rebelled, marched south against Luoyang, and usurped a false throne.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward An Lushan rebelled, marched south against Luoyang, and proclaimed himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰東守潼關，累月，奏冕為御史中丞，追赴京。

translations.literal: Geshu Han guarded Tong Pass in the east for months, then memorialized appointing Mian Vice Censor-in-Chief and summoning him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han held Tong Pass in the east for months, then memorialized to appoint Mian Vice Censor-in-Chief and summon him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 冕又詰曰：「事驗也。」

translations.literal: Mian questioned him again: "It has been verified."
translations.idiomatic: Mian questioned him again: "It has come true."

sentences.zh: 冕又問三日之兆，梁鳳曰：「東京日即自磨滅，蜀川日亦不能久，此間日何轉分明，不可說。」

translations.literal: Mian asked about the omen of the three days. Liangfeng said: "The sun of the Eastern Capital will soon fade away; the sun of Shu cannot last long either; as for the sun between them, how it grows clearer—I cannot speak of it."
translations.idiomatic: Mian asked about the omen of the three days. Liangfeng said, "The sun over the Eastern Capital will soon fade away; the sun over Shu cannot endure either; as for the sun between them—how it grows ever clearer—I cannot speak of that."

sentences.zh: 冕志之。

translations.literal: Mian noted this.
translations.idiomatic: Mian committed this to memory.

sentences.zh: 既潼關失守，玄宗幸蜀，肅宗北如靈武，冕會之，勸成策立，改元為至德元年。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass fell, Xuanzong fled to Shu and Suzong went north to Lingwu; Mian joined him, urged the enthronement, and the era name was changed to the first year of Zhide.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Pass fell, Xuanzong fled to Shu and Suzong went north to Lingwu; Mian joined him, urged the proclamation of a new reign, and the era name was changed to the first year of Zhide.

sentences.zh: 冕果為中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: Mian did indeed become Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Mian did indeed become Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 冕奏之，肅宗召拜都水使者。

translations.literal: Mian reported this, and Suzong summoned Liangfeng and appointed him Director of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Mian reported this to the throne, and Suzong summoned Liangfeng and appointed him Director of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 梁鳳在河隴，謂呂諲曰：「判官骨相，合得宰相。

translations.literal: In the He-Long region Liangfeng said to Lü Yun: "From the bone structure of your face, Sir, you are fit to become chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: While in the He-Long region, Liangfeng said to Lü Yun, "From the bone structure of your face, Sir, you are destined to become chancellor.

sentences.zh: 須得一大驚怖，即得。」

translations.literal: You need one great shock of terror, and then you will attain it."
translations.idiomatic: You need one great shock of terror, and then you will attain it."

sentences.zh: 諲後至驛，責讓驛長，搒之。

translations.literal: Later Yun arrived at a post station, rebuked the station chief, and had him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yun arrived at a post station, rebuked the station chief, and had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 驛吏武將，性粗猛，持弓矢突入，射諲，矢兩發，幾中諲面，諲逾牆得免。

translations.literal: The station's military attendant was coarse and fierce; grasping bow and arrows he burst in and shot at Yun—two arrows, nearly striking his face; Yun scaled a wall and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The station's military attendant was coarse and fierce; seizing bow and arrows he burst in and shot at Yun—two arrows, nearly striking his face—and Yun scaled a wall and escaped.

sentences.zh: 以報梁鳳，梁鳳曰：「此必入相。」

translations.literal: When this was reported to Liangfeng, he said: "This man will surely enter the chancellorship."
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported to Liangfeng, he said, "This man will surely enter the chancellorship."

sentences.zh: 逾年，諲自黃門侍郎知政事。

translations.literal: A year later Yun rose from Vice Director of the Gate of Yellow to administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Yun rose from Vice Director of the Gate of Yellow to administer state affairs.

sentences.zh: 梁鳳在鳳翔，李揆、盧允二人同見之，俱素服，自稱選人。

translations.literal: At Fengxiang, Li Kui and Lu Yun both visited Liangfeng together, all in plain dress, calling themselves examination candidates.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang, Li Kui and Lu Yun visited Liangfeng together, both in plain dress and calling themselves examination candidates.

sentences.zh: 梁鳳謂之曰：「公等並至清望官，那得雲無官。」

translations.literal: Liangfeng said to them: "You are both men of the highest repute—how can you say you hold no office?"
translations.idiomatic: Liangfeng said to them, "You are both men of the highest repute—how can you claim to hold no office?"

sentences.zh: 揆、允以實對。

translations.literal: Kui and Yun answered truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and Yun answered truthfully.

sentences.zh: 梁鳳遣二人行，謂揆曰：「公從舍人即入相，一年內事。」

translations.literal: Liangfeng sent the two on their way and said to Kui: "Sir, from Drafting Attendant you will enter the chancellorship—all within one year."
translations.idiomatic: Liangfeng sent the two on their way and said to Kui, "Sir, from Drafting Attendant you will enter the chancellorship—all within one year."

sentences.zh: 謂允曰：「公好即是吏部郎中。」

translations.literal: To Yun he said: "Sir, your next post will be Director in the Ministry of Personnel."
translations.idiomatic: To Yun he said, "Sir, your next post will be Director in the Ministry of Personnel."

sentences.zh: 及克復兩京，揆自中書舍人知禮部侍郎事，入為中書侍郎、平章事，乃以允為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, Kui went from Zhongshu Sheren overseeing the Vice Ministry of Rites to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, and Yun was made Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were recovered, Kui rose from Secretariat Drafter overseeing the Vice Ministry of Rites to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, and Yun was appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 其驗多此類。

translations.literal: Verifications of this sort were many.
translations.idiomatic: Predictions of this sort were fulfilled again and again.

sentences.zh: 爾後佯聾以自晦。

translations.literal: Afterward he feigned deafness to hide himself.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he feigned deafness to conceal himself.

sentences.zh: 冕為右僕射、兼御史大夫、成都尹、劍南節度使，有進止，令將梁鳳行。

translations.literal: When Mian became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Prefect of Chengdu, and military commissioner of Jiannan, on his departures and arrivals he had Liangfeng accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Prefect of Chengdu, and military commissioner of Jiannan, he had Liangfeng accompany him whenever he traveled.

sentences.zh: 後乃病卒。

translations.literal: Later he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 張果者，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Guo—no one knew where he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guo—no one knew where he came from.

sentences.zh: 則天時，隱於中條山，往來汾、晉間，時人傳其有長年秘術，自雲年數百歲矣。

translations.literal: During Wu Zetian's reign he hid on Zhongtiao Mountain, traveling between Fen and Jin; people said he possessed secret arts of longevity and claimed to be several hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: During Wu Zetian's reign he hid on Zhongtiao Mountain, traveling between Fen and Jin; people said he possessed secret arts of longevity and claimed to be several hundred years old.

sentences.zh: 嘗著《陰符經玄解》，盡其玄理。

translations.literal: He once authored An Esoteric Commentary on the Classic of the Hidden Talisman, exhaustively treating its arcane principles.
translations.idiomatic: He once authored An Esoteric Commentary on the Classic of the Hidden Talisman, exhaustively treating its arcane principles.

sentences.zh: 則天遣使召之，果佯死不赴。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian sent envoys to summon him; Guo feigned death and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian sent envoys to summon him; Guo feigned death and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 後人復見之，往來恆州山中。

translations.literal: Later people saw him again, traveling in the mountains of Heng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later people saw him again, traveling in the mountains of Heng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元二十一年，恆州刺史韋濟以狀奏聞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan, Prefect Wei Ji of Heng submitted a report.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan, Prefect Wei Ji of Heng submitted a report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令通事舍人裴晤往迎之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered Attendant of Affairs Pei Wu to go and escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong ordered Attendant of Affairs Pei Wu to go and escort him to court.

sentences.zh: 果對使絕氣如死，良久漸蘇。

translations.literal: Guo stopped breathing before the envoy as if dead; after a long while he gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: Guo stopped breathing before the envoy as if dead; after a long while he gradually revived.

sentences.zh: 晤不敢逼，馳還奏狀。

translations.literal: Wu dared not press him and galloped back to report.
translations.idiomatic: Wu dared not press him and galloped back to report.

sentences.zh: 又遣中書舍人徐嶠齎璽書以邀迎之。

translations.literal: He again sent Zhongshu Sheren Xu Qiao bearing an imperial seal letter to invite him.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Secretariat Drafter Xu Qiao bearing an imperial seal letter to invite him.

sentences.zh: 果乃隨嶠至東都，肩輿入東宮中。

translations.literal: Guo then followed Qiao to the Eastern Capital and was carried in a sedan chair into the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Guo then followed Qiao to the Eastern Capital and was carried in a sedan chair into the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初即位，親訪理道及神仙方藥之事，及聞變化不測而疑之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong first took the throne he personally inquired into the Way of governance and matters of immortals and elixirs; hearing of Guo's unpredictable transformations, he grew doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong first took the throne he personally inquired into the Way of governance and matters of immortals and elixirs; hearing of Guo's unpredictable transformations, he grew doubtful.

sentences.zh: 有邢和璞者，善算人而知夭壽善惡。

translations.literal: There was Xing Hehu, skilled at calculating people's fates and knowing their span of life and good or ill fortune.
translations.idiomatic: There was Xing Hehu, skilled at calculating people's fates and discerning their span of life and whether their fortune would be good or ill.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令算果，則懵然莫知其甲子。

translations.literal: Xuanzong had him calculate Guo's fate; he was utterly blank and could not determine his birth year.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had him calculate Guo's fate; he was utterly baffled and could not determine his birth year.

sentences.zh: 又有師夜光者，善視鬼。

translations.literal: There was also Master Yeguang, skilled at seeing ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Master Yeguang, skilled at seeing ghosts.

sentences.zh: 玄宗召果與之密坐，令夜光視之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong summoned Guo and had him sit privately with Yeguang, ordering Yeguang to look at him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong summoned Guo and had him sit privately with Yeguang, ordering Yeguang to look at him.

sentences.zh: 夜光進曰：「果今安在？」

translations.literal: Yeguang stepped forward and said: "Where is Guo now?"
translations.idiomatic: Yeguang stepped forward and said, "Where is Guo now?"

sentences.zh: 夜光對面終莫能見。

translations.literal: Facing him directly to the end, Yeguang could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Face to face with him, Yeguang could not see him at all.

sentences.zh: 玄宗謂力士曰：「吾聞飲堇汁無苦者，真奇士也。」

translations.literal: Xuanzong said to Lishi: "I have heard that one who drinks hellebore juice without bitterness is a true marvel."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong said to Lishi, "I have heard that one who drinks hellebore juice without tasting bitterness is a true marvel."

sentences.zh: 會天寒，使以堇汁飲果。

translations.literal: It happened to be cold; he had Guo drink hellebore juice.
translations.idiomatic: It happened to be cold weather; he had Guo drink hellebore juice.

sentences.zh: 果乃引飲三卮，醺然如醉所作，顧曰：「非佳酒也。」

translations.literal: Guo drank three cups, swaying as if drunk, and turning said: "This is not fine wine."
translations.idiomatic: Guo drank three cups, swaying as if drunk, and turning said, "This is not fine wine."

sentences.zh: 乃寢。

translations.literal: Then he slept.
translations.idiomatic: Then he slept.

sentences.zh: 頃之，取鏡視齒，則盡燋且黧。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he took a mirror to look at his teeth—they were all charred and blackened.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, he took a mirror to look at his teeth—they were all charred and blackened.

sentences.zh: 命左右取鐵如意擊齒墜，藏於帶。

translations.literal: He ordered attendants to take an iron ruyi scepter, knock his teeth out, and hide them in his belt.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered attendants to take an iron ruyi scepter, knock his teeth out, and hide them in his belt.

sentences.zh: 乃懷中出神仙藥，微紅，傅墜齒之齗。

translations.literal: Then from his bosom he produced an immortal medicine, faintly red, and applied it to the sockets of the fallen teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Then from his bosom he produced an immortal medicine, faintly red, and applied it to the sockets of the fallen teeth.

sentences.zh: 復寐良久，齒皆出矣，粲然潔白，玄宗方信之。

translations.literal: After sleeping again for a long while, all his teeth had grown back, bright and clean white; only then did Xuanzong believe.
translations.idiomatic: After sleeping again for a long while, all his teeth had grown back, bright and clean white; only then did Xuanzong believe.

sentences.zh: 玄宗好神仙，而欲果尚公主。

translations.literal: Xuanzong loved immortals and wished to marry Guo to a princess.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong loved immortals and wished to marry Guo to a princess.

sentences.zh: 果固未知之，謂秘書少監王迥質、太常少卿蕭華曰：「諺雲娶婦得公主，真可畏也。」

translations.literal: Guo did not yet know this; he said to Secretary Director Wang Huizhi and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xiao Hua: "The proverb says marrying and getting a princess is truly fearsome."
translations.idiomatic: Guo did not yet know this; he said to Secretary Director Wang Huizhi and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xiao Hua, "The proverb says that marrying and getting a princess is truly fearsome."

sentences.zh: 迥質與華相顧，未曉其言。

translations.literal: Huizhi and Hua looked at each other, not understanding his words.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi and Hua looked at each other, not understanding what he meant.

sentences.zh: 即有中使至，宣曰：「玉真公主早歲好道，欲降先生。」

translations.literal: Immediately a palace envoy arrived and announced: "Princess Yuzhen has loved the Way since her youth and wishes to descend to marry the Master."
translations.idiomatic: Immediately a palace envoy arrived and announced, "Princess Yuzhen has loved the Way since her youth and wishes to descend and marry the Master."

sentences.zh: 果大笑，竟不奉詔。

translations.literal: Guo laughed loudly and ultimately did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Guo laughed loudly and ultimately refused the edict.

sentences.zh: 迥質等方悟向來之言。

translations.literal: Only then did Huizhi and the others understand his earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Huizhi and the others understand what he had meant earlier.

sentences.zh: 後懇辭歸山，因下制曰：「恆州張果先生，游方外者也。

translations.literal: Later he earnestly begged leave to return to the mountains; an edict was issued: "Master Zhang Guo of Heng prefecture is one who wanders beyond the mundane world.
translations.idiomatic: Later he earnestly begged leave to return to the mountains; an edict was issued: "Master Zhang Guo of Heng prefecture is one who wanders beyond the mundane world.

sentences.zh: 跡先高尚，深入窈冥。

translations.literal: His track was lofty from the first, plunging deep into the hidden dark.
translations.idiomatic: His path was lofty from the first, plunging deep into the hidden dark.

sentences.zh: 是渾光塵，應召城闕。

translations.literal: He blends light and dust alike, answering the summons to the capital gates.
translations.idiomatic: Though he blended with light and dust alike, he answered the summons to the imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 莫詳甲子之數，且謂羲皇上人。

translations.literal: No one could ascertain the count of his sexagenary cycle; they called him a man of the age of Fuxi.
translations.idiomatic: No one could determine his birth year; they called him a man from the age of Fuxi himself.

sentences.zh: 問以道樞，盡會宗極。

translations.literal: When questioned on the pivot of the Way, he fully comprehended its ultimate principle.
translations.idiomatic: When questioned on the pivot of the Way, he fully grasped its ultimate principle.

sentences.zh: 今特行朝禮，爰畀寵命。

translations.literal: Now he is specially granted court ceremony and bestowed favored rank.
translations.idiomatic: Now he is specially granted an audience at court and honored with a favored appointment.

sentences.zh: 可銀青光祿大夫，號曰通玄先生。」

translations.literal: He may be made Silver-and-Purple Gleaming Light Grand Master of the Palace and styled Master of Penetrating Mystery."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Silver-and-Purple Gleaming Light Grand Master of the Palace and styled Master of Penetrating Mystery."

sentences.zh: 其年請入恆山，錫以衣服及雜彩等，便放歸山。

translations.literal: That year he requested entry to Mount Heng; gifts of clothing and various silks were bestowed, and he was released to return to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: That year he asked to enter Mount Heng; he was given clothing and various silks and then released to return to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 乃入恆山，不知所之。

translations.literal: He then entered Mount Heng, and no one knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Mount Heng, and no one knew where he went.

sentences.zh: 玄宗為造棲霞觀於隱所，在蒲吾縣，後改為平山縣。

translations.literal: Xuanzong had the Qixia Abbey built at his hermitage in Puwu county, later renamed Pingshan county.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had the Qixia Abbey built at his hermitage in Puwu county, later renamed Pingshan county.

sentences.zh: 葉法善

translations.literal: Ye Fashan
translations.idiomatic: Ye Fashan

sentences.zh: 道士葉法善，括州括蒼縣人。

translations.literal: The Daoist Ye Fashan was a native of Kuocang county, Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Ye Fashan was a native of Kuocang county in Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 自曾祖三代為道士，皆有攝養占卜之術。

translations.literal: From his great-grandfather through three generations his family had been Daoists, all skilled in nourishing life and divination.
translations.idiomatic: For three generations from his great-grandfather onward his family had been Daoists, all skilled in nourishing life and divination.
