sentences.zh: 法善少傳符籙，尤能厭劾鬼神。

translations.literal: Fashan in youth inherited talismanic registers and was especially able to suppress and exorcise ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Fashan inherited talismanic registers in his youth and was especially adept at suppressing and exorcising ghosts and spirits.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，高宗聞其名，征詣京師，將加爵位，固辭不受。

translations.literal: During Xianqing, Gaozong heard his name, summoned him to the capital, and was about to confer a noble rank, but he firmly declined and refused it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianqing era, Gaozong heard his name, summoned him to the capital, and was about to confer a noble rank, but Fashan firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 求為道士，因留在內道場，供待甚厚。

translations.literal: He asked to remain a Daoist and was therefore kept in the inner monastery, where he was sumptuously maintained.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to remain a Daoist and was kept in the inner monastery, where he was sumptuously maintained.

sentences.zh: 時高宗令廣征諸方道術之士，合煉黃白。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozong broadly summoned Daoist adepts from all regions to refine gold and silver together.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gaozong broadly summoned Daoist adepts from all regions to work together at transmuting gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 法善上言：「金丹難就，徒費財物，有虧政理，請核其真偽。」

translations.literal: Fashan submitted a memorial: "The golden elixir is hard to achieve; it wastes goods in vain and harms good governance—please verify their truth or falsehood."
translations.idiomatic: Fashan submitted a memorial: "The golden elixir is hard to achieve; it wastes resources in vain and harms good governance—please verify who is genuine and who is not."

sentences.zh: 帝然其言，因令法善試之，由是乃出九十餘人，因一切罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and had Fashan test them; thereby more than ninety men were exposed and all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and had Fashan test them; more than ninety men were exposed and all were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 法善又嘗於東都淩空觀設壇醮祭，城中士女競往觀之。

translations.literal: Fashan also once set up an altar for a communion rite at the Lingkong Abbey in the Eastern Capital; men and women of the city rushed to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Fashan also once set up an altar for a communion rite at the Lingkong Abbey in the Eastern Capital, and men and women of the city flocked to watch.

sentences.zh: 俄頃數十人自投火中，觀者大驚，救之而免。

translations.literal: In a moment dozens of people threw themselves into the fire; onlookers were greatly alarmed and rescued them, so they survived.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment dozens of people threw themselves into the fire; the onlookers were greatly alarmed, but rescued them before any were killed.

sentences.zh: 法善曰：「此皆魅病，為吾法所攝耳。」

translations.literal: Fashan said: "These are all cases of demonic affliction—taken in by my rite, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Fashan said, "These are all cases of demonic affliction—they were taken in by my rite, that is all."

sentences.zh: 問之果然。

translations.literal: When questioned, it proved true.
translations.idiomatic: When questioned, this proved true.

sentences.zh: 法善悉為禁劾，其病乃愈。

translations.literal: Fashan suppressed them all, and their afflictions were cured.
translations.idiomatic: Fashan exorcised them all, and their afflictions were cured.

sentences.zh: 法善自高宗、則天、中宗曆五十年，常往來名山，數召入禁中，盡禮問道。

translations.literal: From Gaozong through Wu Zetian and Zhongzong, spanning fifty years, Fashan often traveled among famous mountains and was repeatedly summoned into the inner palace, where he was treated with full courtesy and questioned on the Way.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozong through Wu Zetian and Zhongzong—spanning fifty years—Fashan often traveled among famous mountains and was repeatedly summoned into the inner palace, where emperors treated him with full courtesy and questioned him on the Way.

sentences.zh: 然排擠佛法，議者或譏其向背。

translations.literal: Yet he rejected Buddhism, and critics sometimes mocked his inconsistency.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he rejected Buddhism, and critics sometimes mocked his inconsistency of purpose.

sentences.zh: 以其術高，終莫之測。

translations.literal: Because his arts were supreme, in the end no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Because his arts were supreme, in the end no one could fathom him.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，稱法善有冥助之力。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he said Fashan had the power of hidden assistance.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, he said Fashan had aided him from beyond the visible world.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，拜鴻臚卿，封越國公，仍依舊為道士，止于京師之景龍觀，又贈其父為歙州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian he was appointed Grand Herald and enfeoffed as Duke of Yue, yet remained a Daoist as before, residing at the Jinglong Abbey in the capital; his father was also posthumously made Prefect of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiantian he was appointed Grand Herald and enfeoffed as Duke of Yue, yet remained a Daoist as before, residing at the Jinglong Abbey in the capital; his father was also posthumously appointed Prefect of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 當時尊寵，莫與為比。

translations.literal: At the time no one could match the honor he received.
translations.idiomatic: At the time no one could match the honor he received.

sentences.zh: 法善生於隋大業之丙子，死於開元之庚子，凡一百七歲。

translations.literal: Fashan was born in the bingzi year of Daye in Sui and died in the gengzi year of Kaiyuan—altogether one hundred and seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Fashan was born in the bingzi year of Daye under Sui and died in the gengzi year of Kaiyuan—altogether one hundred and seven years.

sentences.zh: 八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict said:

sentences.zh: 故道士鴻臚卿、員外置、越國公葉法善，天真精密，妙理玄暢，包括秘要，發揮靈符，固以冥默難源，希夷罕測。

translations.literal: The late Daoist Grand Herald, supernumerary appointment, Duke of Yue Ye Fashan—heavenly in truth and precise in refinement, wondrous in principle and sublime in clarity, encompassing secret essentials and unfurling spirit talismans; truly his silent depth was hard to trace, his rare stillness barely to be measured.
translations.idiomatic: The late Daoist Grand Herald, supernumerary appointment, Duke of Yue Ye Fashan—heavenly in truth and precise in refinement, wondrous in principle and sublime in clarity, encompassing secret essentials and unfurling spirit talismans; truly his silent depth was beyond tracing, his rare stillness barely to be fathomed.

sentences.zh: 而情棲蓬閬，跡混朝伍，保黃冠而不杖，加紫綬而非榮，卓爾孤秀，冷然獨往。

translations.literal: Yet his heart dwelt in thatched retreats and rustic lanes, his track mingled with court ranks; he kept the yellow cap without leaning on a staff, wore the purple sash without taking it as glory—exceptionally lone and outstanding, coolly and alone he went his way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his heart dwelt in thatched retreats and rustic lanes while his track mingled with court ranks; he kept the yellow cap without leaning on a staff and wore the purple sash without taking it as glory—exceptionally lone and outstanding, coolly alone he went his way.

sentences.zh: 勝氣絕俗，貞風無塵，金骨外聳，珠光內應。

translations.literal: Surpassing air beyond the vulgar, upright wind without dust; golden bones protruding outward, pearl-light responding within.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit surpassed the vulgar world, his upright bearing untouched by dust; golden bones showed without, pearl-light answered within.

sentences.zh: 斯乃體應中仙，名升上德。

translations.literal: Thus his body accorded with the middle immortal, his name ascended to the highest virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Thus his body accorded with the middle immortal, his name ascended to the highest virtue.

sentences.zh: 朕當聽政之暇，屢詢至道；

translations.literal: When We have leisure from hearing affairs of state, We have repeatedly inquired into the ultimate Way;
translations.idiomatic: In Our leisure from governing, We have repeatedly inquired into the ultimate Way;

sentences.zh: 公以理國之法，數奏昌言。

translations.literal: you, Sir, on the methods of governing the state have repeatedly presented brilliant counsel.
translations.idiomatic: you, Sir, on the methods of governing the state have repeatedly presented brilliant counsel.

sentences.zh: 謀參隱諷，事宣弘益。

translations.literal: Your plans joined hidden remonstrance; your affairs proclaimed broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Your counsel served as hidden remonstrance; your deeds brought broad benefit.

sentences.zh: 歎徽音之未泯，悲形解之俄留，曾莫憖遺，殲良奄及。

translations.literal: We sigh that your fine tone has not yet faded, yet grieve that your form dissolved so suddenly and remains; never was such virtue spared—goodness has been cut off all at once.
translations.idiomatic: We sigh that your fine voice has not yet faded, yet grieve that your body dissolved so suddenly; such virtue was never spared—goodness has been cut off all at once.

sentences.zh: 永惟平昔，感愴於懷，宜申禮命，式旌泉壤。

translations.literal: Ever mindful of former days, We are moved to grief in Our heart; rites and honors should be extended to proclaim them at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Ever mindful of former days, We are moved to grief; rites and honors should be extended to proclaim them at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 可贈越州都督。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Military Commissioner of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously appointed Military Commissioner of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 僧 玄奘

translations.literal: The Monk Xuanzang
translations.idiomatic: The Monk Xuanzang

sentences.zh: 僧玄奘，姓陳氏，洛州偃師人。

translations.literal: The monk Xuanzang, surname Chen, was a native of Yanshi in Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Xuanzang, surname Chen, was a native of Yanshi in Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 大業末出家，博涉經論。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he left home and broadly studied sutras and treatises.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he left home and broadly studied sutras and treatises.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂翻譯者多有訛謬，故就西域，廣求異本以參驗之。

translations.literal: He once said that translators had many errors and falsehoods; therefore he went to the Western Regions to seek widely for variant texts to compare and verify.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that translators had introduced many errors; therefore he went to the Western Regions to seek widely for variant texts to compare and verify them.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，隨商人往游西域。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he followed merchants to travel the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he followed merchants to travel the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 玄奘既辯博出群，所在必為講釋論難，蕃人遠近咸尊伏之。

translations.literal: Xuanzang was eloquent and learned beyond the crowd; wherever he went he was bound to lecture and debate, and the foreigners near and far all revered and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzang was eloquent and learned beyond the crowd; wherever he went he lectured and debated, and foreigners near and far all revered and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 在西域十七年，經百余國，悉解其國之語，仍采其山川謠俗，土地所有，撰《西域記》十二卷。

translations.literal: In the Western Regions for seventeen years, passing through more than a hundred states, he mastered the language of each state; he also gathered their mountains, rivers, songs, customs, and what the land produced, and composed the Record of the Western Regions in twelve scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Regions for seventeen years, passing through more than a hundred states, he mastered the language of each; he also gathered their geography, songs, customs, and local products, and composed the Record of the Western Regions in twelve scrolls.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十九年，歸至京師。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhenguan he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Zhenguan he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗見之，大悅，與之談論。

translations.literal: Taizong saw him and was greatly pleased, and discoursed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong received him and was greatly pleased, and discoursed with him.

sentences.zh: 於是詔將梵本六百五十七部於弘福寺翻譯，仍敕右僕射房玄齡、太子左庶子許敬宗，廣召碩學沙門五十餘人，相助整比。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the translation at Hongfu Temple of six hundred and fifty-seven fascicles of Sanskrit texts; Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Fang Xuanling and Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Xu Jingzong were also commanded broadly to summon more than fifty eminent scholar-monks to assist in collating and arranging them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict ordered the translation at Hongfu Temple of six hundred and fifty-seven fascicles of Sanskrit texts; Right Vice Director Fang Xuanling and Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Xu Jingzong were also commanded to summon more than fifty eminent scholar-monks to assist in collating them.

sentences.zh: 高宗在宮，為文德太后追福，造慈恩寺及翻經院，內出大幡，敕《九部樂》及京城諸寺幡蓋眾伎，送玄奘及所翻經像、諸高僧等入住慈恩寺。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was still in the palace, to seek merit for Empress Wende he built Cien Temple and a scriptural translation hall; from within the palace great banners were issued, and the Nine-Part Music and banners, canopies, and performers from temples of the capital were commanded to escort Xuanzang and the translated images and eminent monks to take up residence at Cien Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was still in the palace, to seek merit for Empress Wende he built Cien Temple and a scriptural translation hall; from within the palace great banners were issued, and the Nine-Part Music and banners, canopies, and performers from temples of the capital were sent to escort Xuanzang, the translated images, and eminent monks to take up residence at Cien Temple.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，高宗又令左僕射于志寧、侍中許敬宗、中書令來濟、李義府、杜正倫、黃門侍郎薛元超等，共潤色玄奘所定之經，國子博士范義碩、太子洗馬郭瑜、弘文館學士高若思等，助加翻譯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, Gaozong again ordered Left Vice Director Yu Zhining, Palace Attendant Xu Jingzong, Secretariat Directors Lai Ji, Li Yifu, and Du Zhenlun, Vice Secretariat Director Xue Yuanchao, and others jointly to polish the scriptures Xuanzang had settled; Director of the Directorate of Education Fan Yishuo, Groom of the Heir Apparent Guo Yu, and Academician of the Hongwen Institute Gao Ruosi, among others, assisted in further translation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing, Gaozong again ordered Left Vice Director Yu Zhining, Palace Attendant Xu Jingzong, Secretariat Directors Lai Ji, Li Yifu, and Du Zhenlun, Vice Secretariat Director Xue Yuanchao, and others jointly to polish the scriptures Xuanzang had settled; Director of the Directorate of Education Fan Yishuo, Groom of the Heir Apparent Guo Yu, and Academician of the Hongwen Institute Gao Ruosi, among others, assisted in further translation.

sentences.zh: 凡成七十五部。

translations.literal: Altogether seventy-five fascicles were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether seventy-five fascicles were completed.

sentences.zh: 奏上之。

translations.literal: They were submitted to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: They were submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 後以京城人眾競來禮謁，玄奘乃奏請逐靜翻譯，敕乃移於宜君山故玉華宮。

translations.literal: Later, because the people of the capital competed to come pay respects, Xuanzang memorialized requesting a quiet place for translation; an edict then moved the work to the former Yuhua Palace on Mount Yijun.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because crowds in the capital competed to come pay respects, Xuanzang memorialized requesting a quiet place for translation; an edict then moved the work to the former Yuhua Palace on Mount Yijun.

sentences.zh: 六年卒，時年五十六，歸葬于白鹿原，士女送葬者數萬人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged fifty-six; he was buried at Bailuyuan, and tens of thousands of men and women attended the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died at fifty-six; he was buried at Bailuyuan, and tens of thousands of men and women attended the funeral.

sentences.zh: 僧 神秀

translations.literal: The Monk Shenxiu
translations.idiomatic: The Monk Shenxiu

sentences.zh: 僧神秀，姓李氏，汴州尉氏人。

translations.literal: The monk Shenxiu, surname Li, was a native of Weishi in Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Shenxiu, surname Li, was a native of Weishi in Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 少遍覽經史，隋末出家為僧。

translations.literal: In youth he broadly read the classics and histories; at the end of Sui he left home to become a monk.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he broadly read the classics and histories; at the end of the Sui he left home to become a monk.

sentences.zh: 後遇蘄州雙峰山東山寺僧弘忍，以坐禪為業，乃歎伏曰：「此真吾師也。」

translations.literal: Later he encountered the monk Hongren of Dongshan Temple on Twin Peaks in Qizhou, who made seated meditation his practice; he sighed in admiration and said: "This is truly my teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Later he encountered the monk Hongren of Dongshan Temple on Twin Peaks in Qizhou, who made seated meditation his practice; he sighed in admiration and said, "This is truly my teacher."

sentences.zh: 便往事弘忍，專以樵汲自役，以求其道。

translations.literal: He then went to serve Hongren, devoting himself solely to gathering firewood and drawing water to seek the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to serve Hongren, devoting himself solely to gathering firewood and drawing water as he sought the Way.

sentences.zh: 昔後魏末，有僧達摩者，本天竺王子，以護國出家，入南海，得禪宗妙法，雲自釋迦相傳，有衣缽為記，世相付授。

translations.literal: In the late Northern Wei there was a monk named Bodhidharma, originally a prince of Tianzhu; to protect his state he left home, entered the South Sea, and obtained the wondrous method of the Chan school—he said it had been transmitted from Shakyamuni, with robe and bowl as tokens passed down from generation to generation.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Northern Wei there was a monk named Bodhidharma, originally a prince of India; to protect his state he left home, entered the South Sea, and obtained the wondrous method of the Chan school—he said it had been transmitted from Shakyamuni, with robe and bowl as tokens passed down from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 達摩齎衣缽航海而來，至梁，詣武帝。

translations.literal: Bodhidharma carried robe and bowl across the sea and came to Liang, where he went to see Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Bodhidharma carried robe and bowl across the sea and came to Liang, where he went to see Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 帝問以有為之事，達摩不說。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned him on matters of conditioned action; Bodhidharma did not speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him on matters of conditioned action; Bodhidharma would not discuss them.

sentences.zh: 乃之魏，隱于嵩山少林寺，遇毒而卒。

translations.literal: He then went to Wei and hid at Shaolin Temple on Mount Song, where he met poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Wei and hid at Shaolin Temple on Mount Song, where he was poisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 其年，魏使宋雲於蔥嶺回，見之，門徒發其墓，但有衣履而已。

translations.literal: That year, the Wei envoy Song Yun, returning from Congling, saw him; his disciples opened his tomb and found only clothing and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, the Wei envoy Song Yun, returning from the Pamirs, saw him; his disciples opened his tomb and found only clothing and shoes.

sentences.zh: 達摩傳慧可，慧可嘗斷其左臂，以求其法，慧可傳璨，璨傳道信，道信傳弘忍。

translations.literal: Bodhidharma transmitted to Huike; Huike once cut off his left arm to seek the teaching; Huike transmitted to Sengcan, Sengcan to Daoxin, and Daoxin to Hongren.
translations.idiomatic: Bodhidharma transmitted to Huike; Huike once cut off his left arm to seek the teaching; Huike transmitted to Sengcan, Sengcan to Daoxin, and Daoxin to Hongren.

sentences.zh: 弘忍姓周氏，黃梅人。

translations.literal: Hongren's surname was Zhou; he was a native of Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: Hongren's surname was Zhou; he was a native of Huangmei.

sentences.zh: 初，弘忍與道信並住東山寺，故謂其法為東山法門。

translations.literal: At first Hongren and Daoxin both stayed at Dongshan Temple; therefore their teaching was called the Dongshan gate of the Dharma.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hongren and Daoxin both stayed at Dongshan Temple; therefore their teaching was called the Dongshan gate of the Dharma.

sentences.zh: 神秀既師事弘忍，弘忍深器異之，謂曰：「吾度人多矣，至於懸解圓照，無先汝者。」

translations.literal: After Shenxiu took Hongren as teacher, Hongren greatly prized and distinguished him, saying: "Of the many I have brought to deliverance, in suspended understanding and perfect illumination none comes before you."
translations.idiomatic: After Shenxiu became Hongren's disciple, Hongren greatly prized him, saying, "Of the many I have brought to deliverance, in suspended understanding and perfect illumination none comes before you."

sentences.zh: 弘忍以咸亨五年卒，神秀乃往荊州，居於當陽山。

translations.literal: When Hongren died in the fifth year of Xianheng, Shenxiu went to Jingzhou and dwelt on Mount Dangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongren died in the fifth year of Xianheng, Shenxiu went to Jingzhou and dwelt on Mount Dangyang.

sentences.zh: 則天聞其名，追赴都，肩輿上殿，親加跪禮，敕當陽山置度門寺以旌其德。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian heard his name and summoned him to the capital; he was carried in a sedan chair into the hall, and she personally bowed to him on her knees; an edict ordered Dumen Temple built on Mount Dangyang to honor his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian heard his name and summoned him to the capital; he was carried in a sedan chair into the hall, and she personally bowed to him on her knees; an edict ordered Dumen Temple built on Mount Dangyang to honor his virtue.

sentences.zh: 時王公已下及京都士庶，聞風爭來謁見，望塵拜伏，日以萬數。

translations.literal: At the time princes and dukes down to the gentry and common people of the capital, hearing his renown, competed to come pay respects; they bowed prostrate in the dust, numbering tens of thousands a day.
translations.idiomatic: At the time princes and dukes down to the gentry and common people of the capital, hearing his renown, competed to come pay respects; they bowed prostrate in the dust, numbering tens of thousands a day.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，尤加敬異。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, he was especially respected and favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, Shenxiu was especially respected and favored.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人張說嘗問道，執弟子之禮，退謂人曰：「禪師身長八尺，龐眉秀耳，威德巍巍，王霸之器也。」

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Zhang Yue once questioned him on the Way and observed the rites of a disciple; afterward he said to others: "The Chan master is eight feet tall, with sweeping brows and fine ears; his authority and virtue are towering—he has the stuff of kings and hegemons."
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafter Zhang Yue once questioned him on the Way and observed the rites of a disciple; afterward he said to others, "The Chan master is eight feet tall, with sweeping brows and fine ears; his authority and virtue are towering—he has the stuff of kings and hegemons."

sentences.zh: 慧能 普寂 義福 附

translations.literal: Huineng, Puji, and Yifu—Appended
translations.idiomatic: Huineng, Puji, and Yifu—Appended Biographies

sentences.zh: 初，神秀同學僧慧能者，新州人也。

translations.literal: At first Shenxiu's fellow-student the monk Huineng was a native of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shenxiu's fellow-student the monk Huineng was a native of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 與神秀行業相埒。

translations.literal: His practice and attainment rivaled Shenxiu's.
translations.idiomatic: His practice and attainment rivaled Shenxiu's.

sentences.zh: 弘忍卒後，慧能住韶州廣果寺。

translations.literal: After Hongren died, Huineng dwelt at Guangguo Temple in Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongren died, Huineng dwelt at Guangguo Temple in Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 韶州山中，舊多虎豹，一朝盡去，遠近驚歎，咸歸伏焉。

translations.literal: In the mountains of Shaozhou there had been many tigers and leopards; in one morning they all departed, and people near and far marveled and all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountains of Shaozhou there had been many tigers and leopards; in one morning they all departed, and people near and far marveled and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 神秀嘗奏則天，請追慧能赴都，慧能固辭。

translations.literal: Shenxiu once memorialized Wu Zetian, requesting that Huineng be summoned to the capital; Huineng firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu once memorialized Wu Zetian, requesting that Huineng be summoned to the capital; Huineng firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 神秀又自作書重邀之，慧能謂使者曰：「吾形貌短陋，北土見之，恐不敬吾法。

translations.literal: Shenxiu also wrote a letter himself earnestly inviting him; Huineng said to the envoy: "My appearance is short and ugly; if people of the North see me, they may not revere my teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu also wrote a letter himself earnestly inviting him; Huineng said to the envoy, "My appearance is short and ugly; if people of the North see me, they may not revere my teaching.

sentences.zh: 又先師以吾南中有緣，亦不可違也。」

translations.literal: Moreover my former teacher said I had karmic ties in the south, and that too cannot be violated."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my former teacher said I had karmic ties in the south, and that too cannot be violated."

sentences.zh: 竟不度嶺而死。

translations.literal: In the end he did not cross the range and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not cross the mountains and died.

sentences.zh: 天下乃散傳其道，謂神秀為北宗，慧能為南宗。

translations.literal: All under Heaven then spread his teaching separately, calling Shenxiu the Northern school and Huineng the Southern school.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven then spread his teaching separately, calling Shenxiu the Northern school and Huineng the Southern school.

sentences.zh: 神秀以神龍二年卒，士庶皆來送葬。

translations.literal: Shenxiu died in the second year of Shenlong; gentry and commoners all came to the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu died in the second year of Shenlong; gentry and commoners all came to the funeral.

sentences.zh: 有詔賜諡曰「大通禪師」。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed the posthumous title "Chan Master of Great Penetration."
translations.idiomatic: An edict bestowed the posthumous title "Chan Master of Great Penetration."

sentences.zh: 又于相王舊宅置報恩寺，岐王范、張說及征士盧鴻一皆為其碑文。

translations.literal: Ba'en Temple was also established at the former residence of the Prince of Xiang; Prince of Qi Fan, Zhang Yue, and the recluse Lu Hongyi all wrote his epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: Ba'en Temple was also established at the former residence of the Prince of Xiang; Prince of Qi Fan, Zhang Yue, and the recluse Lu Hongyi all wrote his epitaph.

sentences.zh: 神秀卒後，弟子普寂、義福，並為時人所重。

translations.literal: After Shenxiu died, his disciples Puji and Yifu were both highly regarded by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenxiu died, his disciples Puji and Yifu were both highly regarded by people of the time.

sentences.zh: 普寂姓馮氏，蒲州河東人也。

translations.literal: Puji's surname was Feng; he was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Puji's surname was Feng; he was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 年少時遍尋高僧，以學經律。

translations.literal: In youth he sought eminent monks everywhere to study sutras and vinaya.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he sought eminent monks everywhere to study sutras and vinaya.

sentences.zh: 時神秀在荊州玉泉寺，普寂乃往師事，凡六年，神秀奇之，盡以其道授焉。

translations.literal: At the time Shenxiu was at Yuquan Temple in Jingzhou; Puji went to take him as teacher; altogether six years; Shenxiu thought him extraordinary and fully transmitted his teaching to him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shenxiu was at Yuquan Temple in Jingzhou; Puji went to become his disciple; for six years Shenxiu thought him extraordinary and fully transmitted his teaching to him.

sentences.zh: 久視中，則天召神秀至東都，神秀因薦普寂，乃度為僧。

translations.literal: During Jiushi, Wu Zetian summoned Shenxiu to the Eastern Capital; Shenxiu thereupon recommended Puji, and he was ordained as a monk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiushi era, Wu Zetian summoned Shenxiu to the Eastern Capital; Shenxiu thereupon recommended Puji, and he was ordained as a monk.

sentences.zh: 及神秀卒，天下好釋氏者咸師事之。

translations.literal: When Shenxiu died, all under Heaven who loved Buddhism took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenxiu died, all who loved Buddhism under Heaven took Puji as their teacher.

sentences.zh: 中宗聞其高年，特下制令普寂代神秀統其法眾。

translations.literal: Zhongzong heard of his great age and specially issued an edict ordering Puji to succeed Shenxiu in leading the Dharma assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong heard of his great age and specially issued an edict ordering Puji to succeed Shenxiu in leading the Dharma assembly.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，敕普寂于都城居止。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, an edict ordered Puji to reside in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, an edict ordered Puji to reside in the capital.

sentences.zh: 時王公士庶，競來禮謁。

translations.literal: At the time princes, dukes, gentry, and commoners competed to come pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: At the time princes, dukes, gentry, and commoners competed to come pay respects.

sentences.zh: 普寂嚴重少言，來者難見其和悅之容，遠近尤以此重之。

translations.literal: Puji was grave and spoke little; visitors found it hard to see his gentle and pleasant countenance, and people near and far especially honored him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Puji was grave and spoke little; visitors found it hard to see his gentle and pleasant countenance, and people near and far especially honored him for this.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，終於都城興唐寺，年八十九。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died at Xingtang Temple in the capital, aged eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he died at Xingtang Temple in the capital, aged eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 時都城士庶曾謁者，皆制弟子之服。

translations.literal: At the time, gentry and commoners of the capital who had once paid calls all had disciple's robes made.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, all gentry and commoners of the capital who had ever paid him respects had disciple's robes made.

sentences.zh: 有制賜號為「大照禪師」。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed the posthumous title "Chan Master of Great Illumination."
translations.idiomatic: An edict bestowed the posthumous title "Chan Master of Great Illumination."

sentences.zh: 及葬，河南尹裴寬及其妻子，並衰麻列于門徒之次，士庶傾城哭送，閭里為之空焉。

translations.literal: At the burial, Henan Intendant Pei Kuan and his wife, in hemp mourning garments, stood among the disciples; gentry and commoners sent the city out weeping in farewell, and the streets were emptied for it.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial, Henan Intendant Pei Kuan and his wife, in hemp mourning garments, stood among the disciples; gentry and commoners sent the whole city out weeping in farewell, and the streets were emptied.

sentences.zh: 義福姓薑氏，潞州銅鞮人。

translations.literal: Yifu's surname was Jiang; he was a native of Tongdi in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu's surname was Jiang; he was a native of Tongdi in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 初止藍田化感寺，處方丈之室，凡二十餘年，未嘗出宇之外。

translations.literal: At first he stayed at Huagan Temple in Lantian, occupying the abbot's quarters; for more than twenty years he never stepped outside the temple precinct.
translations.idiomatic: At first he stayed at Huagan Temple in Lantian, occupying the abbot's quarters; for more than twenty years he never stepped outside the temple precinct.

sentences.zh: 後隸京城慈恩寺。

translations.literal: Later he was affiliated with Cien Temple in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was affiliated with Cien Temple in the capital.

sentences.zh: 開元十一年，從駕往東都，途經蒲、虢二州，刺史及官吏士女，皆齎幡花迎之，所在途路充塞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, accompanying the emperor to the Eastern Capital, passing through Pu and Guo prefectures, prefects and officials, gentry and women all brought banners and flowers to welcome him, filling the roads wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, accompanying the emperor to the Eastern Capital, he passed through Pu and Guo prefectures; prefects, officials, gentry, and common folk all brought banners and flowers to welcome him, and the roads were packed wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 以二十年卒，有制賜號「大智禪師」。

translations.literal: He died in the twentieth year; an edict bestowed the posthumous title "Chan Master of Great Wisdom."
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year; an edict bestowed the posthumous title "Chan Master of Great Wisdom."

sentences.zh: 葬于伊闕之北，送葬者數萬人。

translations.literal: He was buried north of Yique; tens of thousands attended the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried north of Yique; tens of thousands attended the funeral.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎嚴挺之為制碑文。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Tingzhi composed his epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Tingzhi composed his epitaph.

sentences.zh: 神秀，禪門之傑，雖有禪行，得帝王重之，而未嘗聚徒開堂傳法。

translations.literal: Shenxiu was an outstanding figure of the Chan school; though he had Chan practice and won imperial favor, he never gathered disciples, opened a hall, and transmitted the Dharma.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu was an outstanding figure of the Chan school; though he had Chan practice and won imperial favor, he never gathered disciples in a hall to transmit the Dharma.

sentences.zh: 至弟子普寂，始於都城傳教，二十餘年，人皆仰之。

translations.literal: It was only with his disciple Puji that teaching was first transmitted in the capital; for more than twenty years all looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: It was only with his disciple Puji that teaching was first transmitted in the capital; for more than twenty years all looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 僧一行

translations.literal: The monk Yixing
translations.idiomatic: The monk Yixing

sentences.zh: 僧一行，姓張氏，先名遂，魏州昌樂人，襄州都督、郯國公公謹之孫也。

translations.literal: The monk Yixing, surname Zhang, formerly named Sui, was a native of Changle in Weizhou, grandson of Gongjian, Regional Commander of Xiangzhou and Duke of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Yixing, surname Zhang, formerly named Sui, was a native of Changle in Weizhou, grandson of Gongjian, Regional Commander of Xiangzhou and Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 父擅，武功令。

translations.literal: His father Shan was magistrate of Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shan was magistrate of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 一行少聰敏，博覽經史，尤精曆象、陰陽、五行之學。

translations.literal: Yixing was clever from youth, widely read in classics and histories, and especially skilled in calendrical astronomy, yin-yang doctrine, and the study of the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing was clever from youth, widely read in classics and histories, and especially skilled in calendrical astronomy, yin-yang doctrine, and the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 時道士尹崇博學先達，素多墳籍。

translations.literal: At the time the Daoist Yin Chong was a learned elder of long standing, always rich in ancient texts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Daoist Yin Chong was a learned elder of long standing, always rich in ancient texts.

sentences.zh: 一行詣崇，借揚雄《太玄經》，將歸讀之。

translations.literal: Yixing went to Chong and borrowed Yang Xiong's Classic of Supreme Mystery to take home and read.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing went to Chong and borrowed Yang Xiong's Classic of Supreme Mystery to take home and read.

sentences.zh: 數日，復詣崇，還其書。

translations.literal: After several days he went again to Chong and returned the book.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he went again to Chong and returned the book.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「此書意指稍深，吾尋之積年，尚不能曉，吾子試更研求，何遽見還也？」

translations.literal: Chong said: "The meaning of this book runs rather deep; I have sought it for years and still cannot understand it. You might try to pursue it further—why return it so soon?"
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "The meaning of this book runs rather deep; I have sought it for years and still cannot understand it. You might try to pursue it further—why return it so soon?"

sentences.zh: 一行曰：「究其義矣。」

translations.literal: Yixing said: "I have plumbed its meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Yixing said, "I have plumbed its meaning."

sentences.zh: 因出所撰《大衍玄圖》及《義決》一卷以示崇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he produced the Chart of the Great Evolution's Mystery and a one-scroll Explication of Its Meaning that he had composed and showed them to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he produced the Chart of the Great Evolution's Mystery and a one-scroll Explication of Its Meaning that he had composed and showed them to Chong.

sentences.zh: 崇大驚，因與一行談其奧賾，甚嗟伏之。

translations.literal: Chong was greatly startled; he then discussed its deepest subtleties with Yixing and deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was greatly startled; he then discussed its deepest subtleties with Yixing and deeply admired him.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「此後生顏子也。」

translations.literal: He said to others: "This young man is a Yan Hui reborn."
translations.idiomatic: He said to others, "This young man is a Yan Hui reborn."

sentences.zh: 一行由是大知名。

translations.literal: From this Yixing became greatly renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From this Yixing became greatly renowned.

sentences.zh: 武三思慕其學行，就請與結交，一行逃匿以避之。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi admired his learning and conduct and sought to befriend him; Yixing hid himself to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi admired his learning and conduct and sought his friendship; Yixing hid himself to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 尋出家為僧，隱於嵩山，師事沙門普寂。

translations.literal: Soon he left home and became a monk, hiding on Mount Song and taking the monk Puji as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left home and became a monk, hiding on Mount Song and taking the monk Puji as teacher.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，敕東都留守韋安石以禮征。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, an edict ordered Eastern Capital Regent Wei Anshi to summon him with proper ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, an edict ordered Eastern Capital Regent Wei Anshi to summon him with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 一行固辭以疾，不應命。

translations.literal: Yixing firmly declined on grounds of illness and did not answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing firmly declined on grounds of illness and did not answer the summons.

sentences.zh: 後步往荊州當陽山，依沙門悟真以習梵律。

translations.literal: Later he walked to Mount Dangyang in Jingzhou and studied Buddhist precepts under the monk Wuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Later he walked to Mount Dangyang in Jingzhou and studied Buddhist precepts under the monk Wuzhen.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，玄宗令其族叔禮部郎中洽齎敕書就荊州強起之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, Xuanzong had his clansman the Ministry of Rites Bureau Director Qia carry an imperial letter to Jingzhou and forcibly summon him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, Xuanzong had his clansman the Ministry of Rites Bureau Director Qia carry an imperial letter to Jingzhou and forcibly summon him.

sentences.zh: 一行至京，置於光太殿，數就之，訪以安國撫人之道，言皆切直，無有所隱。

translations.literal: When Yixing reached the capital he was placed in Guangtai Hall; the emperor repeatedly visited him and questioned him on the way to secure the state and soothe the people; his words were all forthright and candid, with nothing held back.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixing reached the capital he was placed in Guangtai Hall; the emperor repeatedly visited him and questioned him on the way to secure the state and soothe the people; his words were all forthright, with nothing held back.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，永穆公主出降，敕有司優厚發遣，依太平公主故事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, when Princess Yongmu went forth in marriage, an edict ordered the relevant offices to send her off with generous provisions, following the precedent of Princess Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, when Princess Yongmu went forth in marriage, an edict ordered the relevant offices to send her off with generous provisions, following the precedent of Princess Taiping.

sentences.zh: 一行以為高宗末年，唯有一女，所以特加其禮。

translations.literal: Yixing held that in Gaozong's later years the emperor had only one daughter, and for that reason her rites had been specially enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing held that in Gaozong's later years the emperor had only one daughter, and for that reason her rites had been specially enlarged.

sentences.zh: 又太平驕僭，竟以得罪，不應引以為例。

translations.literal: Moreover Taiping had been arrogant and overstepped her place, and in the end was punished for it; her case should not be cited as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Taiping had been arrogant and overstepped her place, and in the end was punished for it; her case should not be cited as precedent.

sentences.zh: 上納其言，遽追敕不行，但依常禮。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words, promptly revoked the edict, and followed only the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his words, promptly revoked the edict, and followed only the usual rites.

sentences.zh: 其諫諍皆此類也。

translations.literal: His remonstrances were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His remonstrances were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 一行尤明著述，撰《大衍論》三卷，《攝調伏藏》十卷，《天一太一經》及《太一局遁甲經》、《釋氏系錄》各一卷。

translations.literal: Yixing was especially accomplished in authorship; he wrote the Great Evolution Treatise in three scrolls, the Compendium of Regulation and the Suppressed Treasury in ten scrolls, and one scroll each of the Scripture of the Heavenly One and Grand One, the Scripture of the Grand One Board and Hidden Stems Escapes, and the Genealogical Record of the Buddhist Lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing was especially accomplished in authorship; he wrote the Great Evolution Treatise in three scrolls, the Compendium of Regulation and the Suppressed Treasury in ten scrolls, and one scroll each of the Scripture of the Heavenly One and Grand One, the Scripture of the Grand One Board and Hidden Stems Escapes, and the Genealogical Record of the Buddhist Lineage.

sentences.zh: 時《麟德歷經》推步漸疏，敕一行考前代諸家曆法，改撰新曆，又令率府長史梁令瓚等與工人創造黃道游儀，以考七曜行度，互相證明。

translations.literal: At the time the Lindé Calendar Scripture had grown gradually loose in its calculations; an edict ordered Yixing to examine the calendar methods of various schools in former ages and compile a new calendar; he was also ordered, together with Chief Secretary of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Liang Lingzan and craftsmen, to create a yellow-path traveling instrument to measure the courses of the seven luminaries and verify one another.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Lindé Calendar Scripture had grown gradually loose in its calculations; an edict ordered Yixing to examine the calendar methods of various schools in former ages and compile a new calendar; he was also ordered, together with Chief Secretary of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Liang Lingzan and craftsmen, to create a yellow-path traveling instrument to measure the courses of the seven luminaries and verify one another.

sentences.zh: 於是一行推《周易》大衍之數，立衍以應之，改撰《開元大衍歷經》。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yixing derived the numbers of the Great Evolution from the Book of Changes, established the evolution to correspond to them, and compiled the Kaiyuan Great Evolution Calendar Scripture.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yixing derived the numbers of the Great Evolution from the Book of Changes, established the evolution to correspond to them, and compiled the Kaiyuan Great Evolution Calendar Scripture.

sentences.zh: 至十五年卒，年四十五，賜諡曰「大慧禪師」。

translations.literal: He died in the fifteenth year, aged forty-five; the posthumous title "Chan Master of Great Wisdom" was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year, aged forty-five; the posthumous title "Chan Master of Great Wisdom" was bestowed.

sentences.zh: 初，一行從祖東台舍人太素，撰《後魏書》一百卷，其《天文志》未成，一行續而成之。

translations.literal: At first Yixing's grand-uncle the Secretariat Drafter of the Eastern Terrace Taisu compiled the Book of Later Wei in one hundred scrolls; its Monograph on Astronomy was unfinished, and Yixing continued and completed it.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yixing's grand-uncle the Secretariat Drafter of the Eastern Terrace Taisu compiled the Book of Later Wei in one hundred scrolls; its Monograph on Astronomy was unfinished, and Yixing continued and completed it.

sentences.zh: 上為一行制碑文，親書于石，出內庫錢五十萬，為起塔於銅人之原。

translations.literal: The emperor composed an epitaph for Yixing and personally wrote it on stone; five hundred thousand in cash from the inner treasury was expended to erect a pagoda for him on Tongren Plain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed an epitaph for Yixing and personally wrote it on stone; five hundred thousand in cash from the inner treasury was expended to erect a pagoda for him on Tongren Plain.

sentences.zh: 明年，幸溫湯，過其塔前，又駐騎徘徊，令品官就塔以告其出豫之意；

translations.literal: The next year, on a visit to the hot springs, passing before his pagoda, the emperor again reined in his horse and lingered, ordering a ranked official to go to the pagoda and tell it of his intent to go out in pleasure;
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on a visit to the hot springs, passing before his pagoda, the emperor again reined in his horse and lingered, ordering a ranked official to go to the pagoda and tell it of his intent to go out in pleasure;

sentences.zh: 更賜絹五十匹，以蒔塔前松柏焉。

translations.literal: He further bestowed fifty bolts of silk to adorn the pine and cypress before the pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: He further bestowed fifty bolts of silk to adorn the pine and cypress before the pagoda.

sentences.zh: 初，一行求訪師資，以窮大衍，至天臺山國清寺，見一院，古松十數，門有流水。

translations.literal: At first, seeking a teacher to exhaust the Great Evolution, Yixing came to Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai; he saw a cloister with a dozen ancient pines and a stream before its gate.
translations.idiomatic: At first, seeking a teacher to exhaust the Great Evolution, Yixing came to Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai; he saw a cloister with a dozen ancient pines and a stream before its gate.

sentences.zh: 一行立於門屏間，聞院僧於庭布算聲，而謂其徒曰：「今日當有弟子自遠求吾演算法，已合到門，豈無人導達也？」

translations.literal: Yixing stood within the gate screen and heard the temple monk in the courtyard casting counting rods, saying to his disciples: "Today a disciple should come from afar seeking my methods of calculation; he ought already to have reached the gate—is there no one to lead him in?"
translations.idiomatic: Yixing stood within the gate screen and heard the temple monk in the courtyard casting counting rods, saying to his disciples, "Today a disciple should come from afar seeking my methods of calculation; he ought already to have reached the gate—is there no one to lead him in?"

sentences.zh: 即除一算。

translations.literal: Thereupon he removed one rod from the count.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he removed one rod from the count.

sentences.zh: 又謂曰：「門前水當卻西流，弟子亦至。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The water before the gate should turn and flow westward; the disciple will also arrive."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The water before the gate should turn and flow westward; the disciple will also arrive."

sentences.zh: 一行承其言而趨入，稽首請法，盡受其術焉，而門前水果卻西流。

translations.literal: Yixing, hearing his words, hurried in, bowed his head and requested the teaching, and fully received his methods; and the water before the gate indeed turned and flowed westward.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing, hearing his words, hurried in, bowed his head and requested the teaching, and fully received his methods; and the water before the gate indeed turned and flowed westward.

sentences.zh: 道士邢和璞嘗謂尹愔曰：「一行其聖人乎？

translations.literal: The Daoist Xing Hepu once said to Yin Yin: "Is Yixing a sage?
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Xing Hepu once said to Yin Yin: "Is Yixing a sage?

sentences.zh: 漢之洛下閎造曆，云：『後八百歲當差一日，必有聖人正之。

translations.literal: Luoxia Hong of Han devised a calendar, saying: 'After eight hundred years it will be off by one day; there must be a sage to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Luoxia Hong of Han devised a calendar, saying: 'After eight hundred years it will be off by one day; there must be a sage to correct it.

sentences.zh: 今年期畢矣，而一行造《大衍》正其差謬，則洛下閎之言，信矣！』

translations.literal: This year the term is complete, and Yixing has compiled the Great Evolution to correct its error; then Luoxia Hong's words are verified!'
translations.idiomatic: This year the term is complete, and Yixing has compiled the Great Evolution to correct its error; then Luoxia Hong's words are verified!'

sentences.zh: 非聖人而何？」

translations.literal: If not a sage, then what?"
translations.idiomatic: If not a sage, then what?"

sentences.zh: 泓師 附

translations.literal: Hongshi—Appended
translations.idiomatic: Hongshi—Appended Biography

sentences.zh: 時又有黃州僧泓者，善葬法。

translations.literal: At the time there was also the monk Hong of Huangzhou, skilled in burial methods.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was also the monk Hong of Huangzhou, skilled in burial methods.

sentences.zh: 每行視山原，即為之圖，張說深信重之。

translations.literal: Whenever he traveled to view hills and plains he would draw maps of them; Zhang Yue deeply trusted and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he traveled to view hills and plains he would draw maps of them; Zhang Yue deeply trusted and valued him.

sentences.zh: 桑道茂

translations.literal: Sang Daomao
translations.idiomatic: Sang Daomao

sentences.zh: 桑道茂者，大曆中游京師，善太一遁甲五行災異之說，言事無不中。

translations.literal: Sang Daomao, during the Dali era traveled in the capital, skilled in the doctrines of the Grand One, Hidden Stems Escapes, and the Five Phases regarding calamities and portents; in whatever he spoke of events, none missed.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Daomao, during the Dali era traveled in the capital, skilled in the doctrines of the Grand One, Hidden Stems Escapes, and the Five Phases regarding calamities and portents; whatever he foretold, none missed.

sentences.zh: 代宗召之禁中，待詔翰林。

translations.literal: Daizong summoned him to the inner palace and kept him as Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong summoned him to the inner palace and kept him as Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 建中初，神策軍修奉天城，道茂請高其垣牆，大為制度，德宗不之省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, when the Shence Army repaired Fengtian city, Daomao requested that its walls be raised higher and its fortifications greatly enlarged; Dezong paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianzhong, when the Shence Army repaired Fengtian city, Daomao requested that its walls be raised higher and its fortifications greatly enlarged; Dezong paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 及硃泚之亂，帝蒼卒出幸，至奉天，方思道茂之言。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci's rebellion broke out, the emperor fled in haste; upon reaching Fengtian he at last recalled Daomao's words.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci's rebellion broke out, the emperor fled in haste; upon reaching Fengtian he at last recalled Daomao's words.

sentences.zh: 時道茂已卒，命祭之。

translations.literal: By then Daomao had already died; the emperor ordered sacrifices performed for him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Daomao had already died; the emperor ordered sacrifices performed for him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：術數之精，事必前知。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When arts of number reach refinement, events are known beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: When arts of number reach refinement, events are known beforehand.

sentences.zh: 粲如垂象，變告無疑。

translations.literal: Brilliant as hung emblems, changes announce themselves without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant as hung emblems, changes announce themselves without doubt.

sentences.zh: 怪誕之夫，誣罔蓍龜。

translations.literal: Men of strange extravagance deceive with milfoil and tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: Men of strange extravagance deceive with milfoil and tortoise.

sentences.zh: 致彼庸妄，幸時艱危。

translations.literal: They bring on the foolish and presumptuous to take advantage of hard and perilous times.
translations.idiomatic: They bring on the foolish and presumptuous to take advantage of hard and perilous times.
